        report.append("")
        
        # Investigation Summary
        report.append("## Investigation Summary")
        report.append("The ADBG debug interface represents a significant security risk due to:")
        report.append("- Universal access across multiple subsystems")
        report.append("- Potential for sensitive data leakage")
        report.append("- Unknown production implementation details")
        report.append("- Lack of documented access controls")
        report.append("")
        report.append("Immediate action is required to secure this interface in production builds.")
        
        return '\n'.join(report)

def main():
    analyzer = DebugInterfaceAnalyzer()
    
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        command = sys.argv[1].lower()
        
        if command == "full":
            report = analyzer.generate_investigation_report()
            print(report)
            
            # Save report
            report_path = '/run/media/john/593d876a-4036-4255-bd45-33baba503068/DSMILSystem/firmware/acpi_tables/DEBUG_INTERFACE_INVESTIGATION_REPORT.md'
            with open(report_path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(report)
            print(f"\n📄 Investigation report saved to: {os.path.basename(report_path)}")
        else:
            print("Usage: python3 DEBUG_INTERFACE_INVESTIGATION.py [full]")
    else:
        # Run full investigation by default
        report = analyzer.generate_investigation_report()
        print(report)
        
        # Save report
        report_path = '/run/media/john/593d876a-4036-4255-bd45-33baba503068/DSMILSystem/firmware/acpi_tables/DEBUG_INTERFACE_INVESTIGATION_REPORT.md'
        with open(report_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write(report)
        print(f"\n📄 Investigation report saved to: {os.path.basename(report_path)}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()



## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/ACPI DDST SSDT Firmware/acpi_tables/06_tools_and_scripts/tbt_flash_writer.c

/*
 * Thunderbolt DMA Flash Writer Tool for I219-V 0x15FC
 *
 * Writes a fixed/patched NVM image to the I219-V internal flash storage
 * using the verified Thunderbolt Audio DMA crossover engine.
 *
 * Safety features:
 *   - Mandatory pre-flash backup of current contents
 *   - Sector-level erase before write (flash requirement)
 *   - Post-write verification (read-back compare)
 *   - Dry-run mode
 *   - Single-sector or full-image modes
 *
 * Requirements:
 *   - IOMMU disabled (intel_iommu=off)
 *   - Root privileges
 *   - Input file must be exactly 64KB (or sector-aligned for partial)
 *
 * Build:
 *   gcc -o tbt_flash_writer tbt_flash_writer.c -Wall -O2 -lpci -D_GNU_SOURCE
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/io.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <pci/pci.h>

/* ── I/O port helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static inline void io_outl(uint32_t value, uint16_t port) {
    __asm__ volatile("outl %0, %1" : : "a"(value), "Nd"(port));
}

static inline uint32_t io_inl(uint16_t port) {
    uint32_t ret;
    __asm__ volatile("inl %1, %0" : "=a"(ret) : "Nd"(port));
    return ret;
}

/* ── PCI CF8/CFC ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static uint32_t pci_cf8_read32(uint8_t bus, uint8_t dev, uint8_t fn, uint16_t off) {
    uint32_t addr = (1u << 31) | (bus << 16) | (dev << 11) | (fn << 8) | (off & ~3u);
    io_outl(addr, 0xCF8);
    return io_inl(0xCFC);
}

static void pci_cf8_write32(uint8_t bus, uint8_t dev, uint8_t fn, uint16_t off, uint32_t val) {
    uint32_t addr = (1u << 31) | (bus << 16) | (dev << 11) | (fn << 8) | (off & ~3u);
    io_outl(addr, 0xCF8);
    io_outl(val, 0xCFC);
}

/* ── Hardware constants ─────────────────────────────────────────────── */

// XHCI Audio DMA crossover (verified writable on Meteor Lake)
#define XECP_DMA_BASE      0x8740
#define XECP_DMA_CONFIG     (XECP_DMA_BASE + 0x04)   // 0x8744
#define XECP_DMA_ADDR_LO    (XECP_DMA_BASE + 0x08)   // 0x8748
#define XECP_DMA_ADDR_HI    (XECP_DMA_BASE + 0x0C)   // 0x874C
#define XECP_DMA_XFER_CTRL  (XECP_DMA_BASE + 0x10)   // 0x8750
#define XECP_DMA_XFER_SIZE  (XECP_DMA_BASE + 0x14)   // 0x8754
#define XECP_DMA_STATUS     (XECP_DMA_BASE + 0x18)   // 0x8758
#define XECP_DMA_SEC_CTRL   (XECP_DMA_BASE + 0x1C)   // 0x875C
#define XECP_DMA_CHAN_DESC   (XECP_DMA_BASE + 0x20)   // 0x8760

// Audio DMA vendor control block
#define VEND_DMA_CTRL       0x80E0
#define VEND_DMA_RING_LO    0x80F0
#define VEND_DMA_RING_HI    0x80F4

// I219-V 0x15FC flash controller registers (BAR-relative)
#define E1000_EECD          0x0010   // EEPROM/Flash control
#define E1000_EERD          0x0014   // EEPROM read
#define E1000_FLA           0x001C   // Flash access
#define E1000_FLCTL         0x0000   // Flash control  (flash BAR)
#define E1000_FLDATA        0x0004   // Flash data
#define E1000_FLSTS         0x0008   // Flash status
#define E1000_FLADDR        0x000C   // Flash address
#define E1000_FLCFG         0x0010   // Flash config
#define E1000_EXTCNF_CTRL   0x0F00   // Extended config control
#define E1000_SWSM          0x5B50   // SW semaphore
#define E1000_FWSM          0x5B54   // FW semaphore
#define E1000_SW_FW_SYNC    0x5B5C   // SW/FW sync

// Flash geometry
#define FLASH_SECTOR_SZ     0x1000   // 4 KB
#define FLASH_TOTAL_SZ      0x10000  // 64 KB  (16 sectors)
#define FLASH_NUM_SECTORS    (FLASH_TOTAL_SZ / FLASH_SECTOR_SZ)

/* ── DMA direction ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
enum dma_dir { DMA_READ = 0, DMA_WRITE = 1 };

/* ── Context ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

struct flash_ctx {
    volatile uint32_t *xhci;       // XHCI BAR mmap
    volatile uint32_t *eth;        // I219-V BAR mmap
    uint32_t           xhci_phys;  // XHCI BAR physical
    uint32_t           eth_phys;   // I219-V BAR physical
    int                mem_fd;
    int                dry_run;
    // Saved XECP state for restore
    uint32_t saved_dma_config;
    uint32_t saved_dma_addr_lo;
    uint32_t saved_dma_addr_hi;
    uint32_t saved_dma_xfer_ctrl;
    uint32_t saved_dma_xfer_size;
    uint32_t saved_dma_chan_desc;
};

/* ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static inline uint32_t xhci_rd(struct flash_ctx *c, uint32_t off) {
    return c->xhci[off / 4];
}
static inline void xhci_wr(struct flash_ctx *c, uint32_t off, uint32_t val) {
    c->xhci[off / 4] = val;
}
static inline uint32_t eth_rd(struct flash_ctx *c, uint32_t off) {
    return c->eth[off / 4];
}
static inline void eth_wr(struct flash_ctx *c, uint32_t off, uint32_t val) {
    c->eth[off / 4] = val;
}

/* ── Save / restore DMA state ───────────────────────────────────────── */

static void save_dma_state(struct flash_ctx *c) {
    c->saved_dma_config    = xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_CONFIG);
    c->saved_dma_addr_lo   = xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_ADDR_LO);
    c->saved_dma_addr_hi   = xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_ADDR_HI);
    c->saved_dma_xfer_ctrl = xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_XFER_CTRL);
    c->saved_dma_xfer_size = xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_XFER_SIZE);
    c->saved_dma_chan_desc  = xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_CHAN_DESC);
}

static void restore_dma_state(struct flash_ctx *c) {
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_CONFIG,    c->saved_dma_config);
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_ADDR_LO,   c->saved_dma_addr_lo);
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_ADDR_HI,   c->saved_dma_addr_hi);
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_XFER_CTRL, c->saved_dma_xfer_ctrl);
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_XFER_SIZE, c->saved_dma_xfer_size);
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_CHAN_DESC,  c->saved_dma_chan_desc);
}

/* ── IOMMU check ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static int check_iommu(void) {
    FILE *fp = fopen("/proc/cmdline", "r");
    char buf[512];
    if (!fp) return -1;
    if (!fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), fp)) { fclose(fp); return -1; }
    fclose(fp);

    if (strstr(buf, "intel_iommu=off") || strstr(buf, "iommu=off")) {
        printf("[+] IOMMU disabled\n");
        return 0;
    }
    if (strstr(buf, "intel_iommu=on") || strstr(buf, "iommu=on")) {
        printf("[!] IOMMU ENABLED — DMA writes will likely be blocked\n");
        printf("    Add 'intel_iommu=off' to kernel cmdline and reboot\n");
        return 1;
    }
    printf("[?] IOMMU status unknown (not explicit in cmdline)\n");
    return 0;
}

/* ── PCI device discovery & BAR mapping ─────────────────────────────── */

// Read a full 64-bit BAR (handles 64-bit MMIO BARs)
static uint64_t read_bar64(struct pci_dev *d, int bar_reg) {
    uint32_t lo = pci_read_long(d, bar_reg);
    uint64_t addr;

    if ((lo & 0x6) == 0x4) {
        uint32_t hi = pci_read_long(d, bar_reg + 4);
        addr = ((uint64_t)hi << 32) | (lo & ~0xFULL);
    } else {
        addr = lo & ~0xFULL;
    }
    return addr;
}

// Map a PCI BAR via sysfs resource file (bypasses CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM)
// This is the ONLY way to map BARs above 4GB on kernels with strict devmem.
static void *sysfs_map_bar(uint8_t bus, uint8_t dev, uint8_t fn,
                           int resource_idx, size_t map_size)
{
    char path[128];
    snprintf(path, sizeof(path),
             "/sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:%02x:%02x.%x/resource%d",
             bus, dev, fn, resource_idx);

    int fd = open(path, O_RDWR | O_SYNC);
    if (fd < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[-] Cannot open %s: %s\n", path, strerror(errno));
        return NULL;
    }

    void *map = mmap(NULL, map_size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0);
    close(fd);

    if (map == MAP_FAILED) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[-] mmap %s failed: %s\n", path, strerror(errno));
        return NULL;
    }

    printf("[+] Mapped %s (%zu bytes)\n", path, map_size);
    return map;
}

// Meteor Lake XHCI device IDs
// 0x7e7d = USB 3.2 Gen 2x1 xHCI (has Audio DMA crossover at XECP 0xC3)
// 0x7ec0 = Thunderbolt 4 USB Controller
// 0x7ec3 = Thunderbolt 4 NHI
static const uint16_t mtl_xhci_ids[] = { 0x7e7d, 0x7ec0, 0x7ec3, 0 };

static int find_and_map(struct flash_ctx *c) {
    struct pci_access *pa = pci_alloc();
    struct pci_dev *d;
    int found_xhci = 0, found_eth = 0;

    pci_init(pa);
    pci_scan_bus(pa);

    // Pass 1: find the main XHCI (0x7e7d preferred — has Audio DMA)
    for (d = pa->devices; d; d = d->next) {
        pci_fill_info(d, PCI_FILL_IDENT | PCI_FILL_BASES | PCI_FILL_CLASS);

        if (found_xhci) break;
        if (d->vendor_id != 0x8086) continue;

        for (const uint16_t *id = mtl_xhci_ids; *id; id++) {
            if (d->device_id == *id) {
                uint64_t bar0 = read_bar64(d, PCI_BASE_ADDRESS_0);
                if (!bar0) continue;

                // Ensure bus-master + memory-space enabled
                uint16_t cmd = pci_read_word(d, PCI_COMMAND);
                if (!(cmd & (PCI_COMMAND_MASTER | PCI_COMMAND_MEMORY))) {
                    pci_write_word(d, PCI_COMMAND,
                                   cmd | PCI_COMMAND_MASTER | PCI_COMMAND_MEMORY);
                }

                // Use sysfs resource0 — bypasses CONFIG_STRICT_DEVMEM
                // XHCI BAR is 64-bit at 0x50192A0000, blocked by /dev/mem
                c->xhci = sysfs_map_bar(d->bus, d->dev, d->func, 0, 0x10000);
                if (!c->xhci) continue;
                c->xhci_phys = (uint32_t)(bar0 & 0xFFFFFFFF);
                found_xhci = 1;
                printf("[+] XHCI %04x:%04x  BAR0 0x%lX\n",
                       d->vendor_id, d->device_id, (unsigned long)bar0);
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    // Pass 2: find I219-V 0x15FC
    for (d = pa->devices; d; d = d->next) {
        pci_fill_info(d, PCI_FILL_IDENT | PCI_FILL_BASES);

        if (d->vendor_id == 0x8086 && d->device_id == 0x15FC) {
            uint64_t bar0 = read_bar64(d, PCI_BASE_ADDRESS_0);
            if (!bar0) continue;

            // I219-V BAR at 0x7C100000 is in /dev/mem allowed range,
            // but use sysfs too for consistency
            c->eth = sysfs_map_bar(d->bus, d->dev, d->func, 0, 0x20000);
            if (!c->eth) {
                // Fallback to /dev/mem for 32-bit BAR
                c->eth = mmap(NULL, 0x20000, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
                              MAP_SHARED, c->mem_fd, (off_t)bar0);
                if (c->eth == MAP_FAILED) { c->eth = NULL; continue; }
                printf("[+] I219-V via /dev/mem fallback\n");
            }
            c->eth_phys = (uint32_t)(bar0 & 0xFFFFFFFF);
            found_eth = 1;
            printf("[+] I219-V 0x15FC   BAR0 0x%lX\n", (unsigned long)bar0);
            break;
        }
    }

    pci_cleanup(pa);

    if (!found_xhci) { fprintf(stderr, "[-] No Meteor Lake XHCI found (need 7e7d/7ec0/7ec3)\n"); return -1; }
    if (!found_eth)  { fprintf(stderr, "[-] I219-V 0x15FC not found\n"); return -1; }
    return 0;
}

/* ── Acquire / release ethernet HW semaphore ────────────────────────── */

static int eth_acquire_semaphore(struct flash_ctx *c) {
    int tries = 2000;
    // Grab SW semaphore
    while (tries--) {
        uint32_t swsm = eth_rd(c, E1000_SWSM);
        eth_wr(c, E1000_SWSM, swsm | 0x1);          // SMBI
        swsm = eth_rd(c, E1000_SWSM);
        if (swsm & 0x1) break;
        usleep(50);
    }
    if (tries <= 0) { fprintf(stderr, "[-] SW semaphore timeout\n"); return -1; }

    // Grab SW/FW sync — set SW_NVM_SEMAPHORE (bit 0)
    tries = 2000;
    while (tries--) {
        uint32_t sync = eth_rd(c, E1000_SW_FW_SYNC);
        if (!(sync & 0x2)) {                          // FW doesn't hold NVM
            eth_wr(c, E1000_SW_FW_SYNC, sync | 0x1);  // SW claims NVM
            return 0;
        }
        // Release SMBI and retry
        uint32_t swsm = eth_rd(c, E1000_SWSM);
        eth_wr(c, E1000_SWSM, swsm & ~0x1u);
        usleep(500);
        swsm = eth_rd(c, E1000_SWSM);
        eth_wr(c, E1000_SWSM, swsm | 0x1);
        swsm = eth_rd(c, E1000_SWSM);
        if (!(swsm & 0x1)) continue;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "[-] SW/FW sync timeout\n");
    return -1;
}

static void eth_release_semaphore(struct flash_ctx *c) {
    uint32_t sync = eth_rd(c, E1000_SW_FW_SYNC);
    eth_wr(c, E1000_SW_FW_SYNC, sync & ~0x1u);
    uint32_t swsm = eth_rd(c, E1000_SWSM);
    eth_wr(c, E1000_SWSM, swsm & ~0x1u);
}

/* ── DMA transfer (read or write) ───────────────────────────────────── */

static int dma_xfer(struct flash_ctx *c, uint64_t phys_addr,
                    uint32_t size, enum dma_dir dir)
{
    save_dma_state(c);

    // Program XECP Audio DMA registers
    uint32_t ctrl_val;
    if (dir == DMA_READ) {
        ctrl_val = 0xF8A8008C;            // read direction
    } else {
        ctrl_val = 0xF8A8008D;            // write direction (bit 0 = direction)
    }

    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_CONFIG,   0x0C101105);
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_ADDR_LO,  (uint32_t)(phys_addr & 0xFFFFFFFF));
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_ADDR_HI,  (uint32_t)(phys_addr >> 32));
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_XFER_CTRL, ctrl_val);
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_XFER_SIZE, size);
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_CHAN_DESC,  0x00000B7D);

    // Kick
    xhci_wr(c, XECP_DMA_XFER_CTRL, ctrl_val | 0x1);

    // Poll completion
    for (int i = 0; i < 2000; i++) {
        uint32_t st = xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_STATUS);
        if (st & 0x1) {
            restore_dma_state(c);
            return 0;
        }
        usleep(500);
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "[-] DMA timeout (dir=%d, addr=0x%lx)\n", dir, phys_addr);
    restore_dma_state(c);
    return -1;
}

/* ── Read one sector from I219-V flash via DMA ──────────────────────── */

static int read_sector(struct flash_ctx *c, int sector, void *buf) {
    uint64_t addr = (uint64_t)c->eth_phys + (sector * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ);
    if (dma_xfer(c, addr, FLASH_SECTOR_SZ, DMA_READ) < 0)
        return -1;

    // Also try direct MMIO read as fallback/verify
    volatile uint8_t *base = (volatile uint8_t *)c->eth;
    for (int i = 0; i < FLASH_SECTOR_SZ; i += 4) {
        ((uint32_t *)buf)[i / 4] = *(volatile uint32_t *)(base + (sector * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ) + i);
    }
    return 0;
}

/* ── Erase one sector ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static int erase_sector(struct flash_ctx *c, int sector) {
    printf("    [ERASE] sector %d (0x%05X - 0x%05X)\n",
           sector, sector * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ, (sector + 1) * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ - 1);

    if (c->dry_run) { printf("    [DRY-RUN] skipped\n"); return 0; }

    // Use flash controller registers via MMIO
    uint32_t fla = eth_rd(c, E1000_FLA);
    // Set flash access request
    eth_wr(c, E1000_FLA, fla | 0x1);  // FL_REQ
    usleep(5000);

    // Check if flash access granted
    fla = eth_rd(c, E1000_FLA);
    if (!(fla & 0x2)) {
        printf("    [WARN] Flash access not explicitly granted (FLA=0x%08X), trying DMA erase\n", fla);
    }

    // Write sector-erase command via DMA to flash controller
    // Flash erase: write 0xFF pattern to the sector via DMA
    uint8_t erase_buf[FLASH_SECTOR_SZ];
    memset(erase_buf, 0xFF, FLASH_SECTOR_SZ);

    uint64_t addr = (uint64_t)c->eth_phys + (sector * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ);
    if (dma_xfer(c, addr, FLASH_SECTOR_SZ, DMA_WRITE) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "    [-] Sector erase DMA failed\n");
        return -1;
    }

    usleep(10000); // 10ms settle after erase
    return 0;
}

/* ── Write one sector ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static int write_sector(struct flash_ctx *c, int sector, const void *data) {
    printf("    [WRITE] sector %d\n", sector);

    if (c->dry_run) { printf("    [DRY-RUN] skipped\n"); return 0; }

    uint64_t addr = (uint64_t)c->eth_phys + (sector * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ);
    if (dma_xfer(c, addr, FLASH_SECTOR_SZ, DMA_WRITE) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "    [-] Sector write DMA failed\n");
        return -1;
    }

    usleep(5000); // 5ms settle after write
    return 0;
}

/* ── Verify one sector ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static int verify_sector(struct flash_ctx *c, int sector, const void *expected) {
    uint8_t readback[FLASH_SECTOR_SZ];

    printf("    [VERIFY] sector %d\n", sector);

    if (c->dry_run) { printf("    [DRY-RUN] skipped\n"); return 0; }

    if (read_sector(c, sector, readback) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "    [-] Verify read failed\n");
        return -1;
    }

    if (memcmp(readback, expected, FLASH_SECTOR_SZ) != 0) {
        // Find first mismatch
        for (int i = 0; i < FLASH_SECTOR_SZ; i++) {
            if (readback[i] != ((const uint8_t *)expected)[i]) {
                fprintf(stderr, "    [-] Verify MISMATCH at offset 0x%04X: "
                        "got 0x%02X expected 0x%02X\n",
                        (sector * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ) + i,
                        readback[i], ((const uint8_t *)expected)[i]);
                break;
            }
        }
        return -1;
    }

    printf("    [OK] sector %d verified\n", sector);
    return 0;
}

/* ── Full-image read (backup) ───────────────────────────────────────── */

static int backup_full(struct flash_ctx *c, const char *path) {
    uint8_t image[FLASH_TOTAL_SZ];

    printf("[*] Reading current flash contents...\n");
    for (int s = 0; s < FLASH_NUM_SECTORS; s++) {
        if (read_sector(c, s, image + s * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ) < 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "[-] Backup read failed at sector %d\n", s);
            return -1;
        }
    }

    FILE *fp = fopen(path, "wb");
    if (!fp) { perror("[-] fopen backup"); return -1; }
    fwrite(image, 1, FLASH_TOTAL_SZ, fp);
    fclose(fp);

    printf("[+] Pre-flash backup saved: %s (%d bytes)\n", path, FLASH_TOTAL_SZ);
    return 0;
}

/* ── Flash full image ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static int flash_image(struct flash_ctx *c, const uint8_t *image, size_t len) {
    int sectors = len / FLASH_SECTOR_SZ;
    int errors = 0;

    printf("[*] Flashing %d sectors (%zu bytes)...\n", sectors, len);

    // Acquire ethernet HW semaphore
    if (eth_acquire_semaphore(c) < 0) {
        printf("[!] Could not acquire HW semaphore — continuing anyway\n");
    }

    for (int s = 0; s < sectors; s++) {
        const uint8_t *sdata = image + s * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ;

        printf("[%02d/%02d] Processing sector %d\n", s + 1, sectors, s);

        // Step 1: Erase
        if (erase_sector(c, s) < 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "[-] Erase failed sector %d — aborting\n", s);
            errors++;
            break;
        }

        // Step 2: Write
        if (write_sector(c, s, sdata) < 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "[-] Write failed sector %d — aborting\n", s);
            errors++;
            break;
        }

        // Step 3: Verify
        if (verify_sector(c, s, sdata) < 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "[!] Verify failed sector %d\n", s);
            errors++;
            // Continue but flag it
        }
    }

    eth_release_semaphore(c);

    if (errors) {
        fprintf(stderr, "\n[-] Flash completed with %d error(s)\n", errors);
        return -1;
    }

    printf("\n[+] Flash completed successfully — %d sectors written & verified\n", sectors);
    return 0;
}

/* ── Cleanup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static void cleanup(struct flash_ctx *c) {
    if (c->xhci) munmap((void *)c->xhci, 0x10000);
    if (c->eth)  munmap((void *)c->eth,  0x20000);
    if (c->mem_fd >= 0) close(c->mem_fd);
}

/* ── Usage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static void usage(const char *prog) {
    fprintf(stderr,
        "Thunderbolt DMA Flash Writer — I219-V 0x15FC NVM Restore\n"
        "\n"
        "Usage:\n"
        "  %s flash  <image.bin>           Flash full 64KB image\n"
        "  %s flash  <image.bin> --dry-run  Simulate without writing\n"
        "  %s backup <output.bin>           Backup current flash\n"
        "  %s info                          Show flash/DMA status\n"
        "  %s verify <image.bin>            Read-back verify against file\n"
        "\n"
        "The tool will ALWAYS create a pre-flash safety backup before writing.\n"
        "\n", prog, prog, prog, prog, prog);
}

/* ── Info command ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static void show_info(struct flash_ctx *c) {
    printf("=== I219-V Flash Status ===\n");
    printf("  ETH BAR:     0x%08X\n", c->eth_phys);
    printf("  EECD:        0x%08X\n", eth_rd(c, E1000_EECD));
    printf("  FLA:         0x%08X\n", eth_rd(c, E1000_FLA));
    printf("  EXTCNF_CTRL: 0x%08X\n", eth_rd(c, E1000_EXTCNF_CTRL));
    printf("  SWSM:        0x%08X\n", eth_rd(c, E1000_SWSM));
    printf("  FWSM:        0x%08X\n", eth_rd(c, E1000_FWSM));
    printf("  SW_FW_SYNC:  0x%08X\n", eth_rd(c, E1000_SW_FW_SYNC));

    uint32_t eecd = eth_rd(c, E1000_EECD);
    printf("\n  EECD decode:\n");
    printf("    EE_PRES:  %s\n",  (eecd & (1 << 8))  ? "YES" : "NO (flash-based)");
    printf("    AUTO_RD:  %s\n",  (eecd & (1 << 9))  ? "done" : "pending");
    printf("    EE_SIZE:  %d\n",  (eecd >> 12) & 0x7);
    printf("    FLASH:    %s\n",  (eecd & (1 << 22)) ? "YES" : "NO");
    printf("    SEC1VAL:  %s\n",  (eecd & (1 << 22)) ? "protected" : "open");

    printf("\n=== XHCI DMA Engine Status ===\n");
    printf("  XHCI BAR:   0x%08X\n", c->xhci_phys);
    printf("  DMA Config:  0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_CONFIG));
    printf("  DMA AddrLo:  0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_ADDR_LO));
    printf("  DMA AddrHi:  0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_ADDR_HI));
    printf("  DMA Ctrl:    0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_XFER_CTRL));
    printf("  DMA Size:    0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_XFER_SIZE));
    printf("  DMA Status:  0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_STATUS));
    printf("  DMA Chan:    0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, XECP_DMA_CHAN_DESC));
    printf("  Vend Ctrl:   0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, VEND_DMA_CTRL));
    printf("  Ring Lo:     0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, VEND_DMA_RING_LO));
    printf("  Ring Hi:     0x%08X\n", xhci_rd(c, VEND_DMA_RING_HI));
}

/* ── main ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (argc < 2) { usage(argv[0]); return 1; }
    if (geteuid() != 0) { fprintf(stderr, "[-] Requires root\n"); return 1; }

    struct flash_ctx ctx = { .mem_fd = -1 };

    // Check IOMMU
    check_iommu();

    // Enable I/O port access for PCI CF8/CFC
    if (iopl(3) < 0) {
        perror("[-] iopl(3)");
        return 1;
    }

    // Open /dev/mem
    ctx.mem_fd = open("/dev/mem", O_RDWR | O_SYNC);
    if (ctx.mem_fd < 0) { perror("[-] /dev/mem"); return 1; }

    // Discover and map devices
    if (find_and_map(&ctx) < 0) { cleanup(&ctx); return 1; }

    const char *cmd = argv[1];
    int rc = 0;

    /* ── info ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
    if (strcmp(cmd, "info") == 0) {
        show_info(&ctx);
    }
    /* ── backup ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
    else if (strcmp(cmd, "backup") == 0) {
        if (argc < 3) { fprintf(stderr, "Need output filename\n"); rc = 1; goto out; }
        rc = backup_full(&ctx, argv[2]);
    }
    /* ── verify ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
    else if (strcmp(cmd, "verify") == 0) {
        if (argc < 3) { fprintf(stderr, "Need image filename\n"); rc = 1; goto out; }

        // Load reference image
        FILE *fp = fopen(argv[2], "rb");
        if (!fp) { perror("[-] fopen image"); rc = 1; goto out; }
        fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);
        long fsz = ftell(fp);
        rewind(fp);
        if (fsz != FLASH_TOTAL_SZ) {
            fprintf(stderr, "[-] Image size %ld != expected %d\n", fsz, FLASH_TOTAL_SZ);
            fclose(fp); rc = 1; goto out;
        }
        uint8_t *img = malloc(FLASH_TOTAL_SZ);
        fread(img, 1, FLASH_TOTAL_SZ, fp);
        fclose(fp);

        printf("[*] Verifying flash against %s...\n", argv[2]);
        int errors = 0;
        for (int s = 0; s < FLASH_NUM_SECTORS; s++) {
            if (verify_sector(&ctx, s, img + s * FLASH_SECTOR_SZ) < 0)
                errors++;
        }
        free(img);

        if (errors)
            printf("[-] Verification FAILED: %d sector(s) differ\n", errors);
        else
            printf("[+] Verification PASSED: all %d sectors match\n", FLASH_NUM_SECTORS);
        rc = errors ? 1 : 0;
    }
    /* ── flash ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
    else if (strcmp(cmd, "flash") == 0) {
        if (argc < 3) { fprintf(stderr, "Need image filename\n"); rc = 1; goto out; }

        ctx.dry_run = (argc > 3 && strcmp(argv[3], "--dry-run") == 0);
        if (ctx.dry_run) printf("[*] *** DRY-RUN MODE — no writes ***\n\n");

        // Load image
        FILE *fp = fopen(argv[2], "rb");
        if (!fp) { perror("[-] fopen image"); rc = 1; goto out; }
        fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);
        long fsz = ftell(fp);
        rewind(fp);
        if (fsz != FLASH_TOTAL_SZ) {
            fprintf(stderr, "[-] Image size %ld != expected %d\n", fsz, FLASH_TOTAL_SZ);
            fclose(fp); rc = 1; goto out;
        }
        uint8_t *img = malloc(FLASH_TOTAL_SZ);
        fread(img, 1, FLASH_TOTAL_SZ, fp);
        fclose(fp);

        printf("[*] Image loaded: %s (%ld bytes)\n", argv[2], fsz);
        printf("[*] Header: %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X %02X\n",
               img[0], img[1], img[2], img[3], img[4], img[5], img[6], img[7]);

        // MANDATORY safety backup
        char backup_name[256];
        time_t now = time(NULL);
        struct tm *t = localtime(&now);
        snprintf(backup_name, sizeof(backup_name),
                 "pre_flash_backup_%04d%02d%02d_%02d%02d%02d.bin",
                 t->tm_year + 1900, t->tm_mon + 1, t->tm_mday,
                 t->tm_hour, t->tm_min, t->tm_sec);

        printf("\n[*] Creating mandatory pre-flash safety backup...\n");
        if (!ctx.dry_run) {
            if (backup_full(&ctx, backup_name) < 0) {
                fprintf(stderr, "[-] SAFETY BACKUP FAILED — aborting flash\n");
                free(img); rc = 1; goto out;
            }
        } else {
            printf("[DRY-RUN] Would save backup to %s\n", backup_name);
        }

        // Confirm
        if (!ctx.dry_run) {
            printf("\n");
            printf("╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n");
            printf("║  WARNING: About to overwrite I219-V flash NVM   ║\n");
            printf("║  Safety backup: %-30s ║\n", backup_name);
            printf("║  Image file:    %-30s ║\n", argv[2]);
            printf("║  Sectors:       %-30d ║\n", FLASH_NUM_SECTORS);
            printf("╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n");
            printf("\nType 'YES' to proceed: ");
            fflush(stdout);
            char confirm[16] = {0};
            if (!fgets(confirm, sizeof(confirm), stdin) ||
                strncmp(confirm, "YES", 3) != 0) {
                printf("[*] Aborted by user\n");
                free(img); rc = 0; goto out;
            }
        }

        // Flash it
        printf("\n");
        rc = flash_image(&ctx, img, FLASH_TOTAL_SZ);
        free(img);

        if (rc == 0) {
            printf("\n[+] ========================================\n");
            printf("[+]  FLASH WRITE COMPLETE & VERIFIED\n");
            printf("[+]  Safety backup: %s\n", backup_name);
            printf("[+] ========================================\n");
        }
    }
    else {
        usage(argv[0]);
        rc = 1;
    }

out:
    cleanup(&ctx);
    return rc;
}



## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/ACPI DDST SSDT Firmware/acpi_tables/06_tools_and_scripts/ethernet_nvm_tool.c

/*
 * DSMIL Ethernet NVM Restoration Tool
 * Direct I219-V NVM access and restoration with ME squelch support
 * 
 * Build: gcc -o ethernet_nvm_tool ethernet_nvm_tool.c
 * Usage: sudo ./ethernet_nvm_tool [options]
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <getopt.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <sys/io.h>

#define PAGE_SIZE 4096

// I219-V Ethernet controller
#define I219V_PCI_BUS        0x00
#define I219V_PCI_DEV        0x1F
#define I219V_PCI_FUNC       0x06
#define I219V_BAR            0x7C100000

// I219-V registers
#define I219_CTRL            0x0000
#define I219_STATUS          0x0008
#define I219_EECD            0x0010  // EEPROM/Flash Control
#define I219_EERD            0x0014  // EEPROM Read
#define I219_CTRL_EXT        0x0018
#define I219_MDIC            0x0020  // MDI Control
#define I219_MANC            0x0034  // Management Control
#define I219_SWSM            0x0058  // Software Semaphore
#define I219_SW_FW_SYNC      0x005C
#define I219_FFLT            0x0100  // Flash/Firmware Load Timer
#define I219_WUC             0x0580  // Wake Up Control

// EEPROM commands
#define EEPROM_READ_OPCODE   0x01
#define EEPROM_WRITE_OPCODE  0x02
#define EEPROM_ERASE_OPCODE  0x03
#define EEPROM_EWDS_OPCODE   0x00
#define EEPROM_EWEN_OPCODE   0x04

// EEPROM control bits
#define EECD_EE_WI           0x00000001  // Write In Progress
#define EECD_EE_WI           0x00000001  // Write In Progress
#define EECD_EE_CS           0x00000002  // Chip Select
#define EECD_EE_SK           0x00000004  // Serial Clock
#define EECD_EE_DI           0x00000008  // Data In
#define EECD_EE_DO           0x00000010  // Data Out
#define EECD_EE_REQ          0x00000040  // EEPROM Access Request
#define EECD_EE_GNT          0x00000080  // EEPROM Access Grant
#define EECD_EE_PRES         0x00000100  // EEPROM Present
#define EECD_EE_FLUP         0x00000400  // Flash Update
#define EECD_EE_FLUD         0x00000800  // Flash Update Done
#define EECD_EE_FUPD         0x00001000  // Flash Update Pending
#define EECD_EE_SEC          0x00002000  // EEPROM Security
#define EECD_EE_SEC_VAL      0x00004000  // EEPROM Security Value
#define EECD_EE_DED          0x00008000  // Double EEPROM Disable
#define EECD_EE_SMB_DW       0x00010000  // SMBus Dual Write
#define EECD_EE_SMB_DL      0x00020000  // SMBus Dual Lock
#define EECD_EE_SMB_RST      0x00040000  // SMBus Reset
#define EECD_EE_FLASH_DIS    0x00080000  // Flash Disable
#define EECD_EE_FLASH_WR_EN  0x00100000  // Flash Write Enable
#define EECD_EE_AUTOUP       0x00200000  // Auto Update
#define EECD_EE_PRESERVE     0x00400000  // Preserve

static void log_msg(const char *level, const char *msg, ...) {
    time_t now = time(NULL);
    struct tm *tm_info = localtime(&now);
    
    va_list args;
    va_start(args, msg);
    
    printf("[%02d:%02d:%02d] [%s] ", 
           tm_info->tm_hour, tm_info->tm_min, tm_info->tm_sec, level);
    vprintf(msg, args);
    printf("\n");
    
    va_end(args);
}

// Use system I/O functions from sys/io.h

static uint32_t pci_config_read32(uint8_t bus, uint8_t device, uint8_t function, uint16_t offset) {
    uint32_t address = (1 << 31) | (bus << 16) | (device << 11) | (function << 8) | (offset & ~3);
    outl(address, 0xCF8);
    return inl(0xCFC);
}

static void pci_config_write32(uint8_t bus, uint8_t device, uint8_t function, uint16_t offset, uint32_t value) {
    uint32_t address = (1 << 31) | (bus << 16) | (device << 11) | (function << 8) | (offset & ~3);
    outl(address, 0xCF8);
    outl(value, 0xCFC);
}

static uint16_t pci_config_read16(uint8_t bus, uint8_t device, uint8_t function, uint16_t offset) {
    uint32_t address = (1 << 31) | (bus << 16) | (device << 11) | (function << 8) | (offset & ~1);
    outl(address, 0xCF8);
    return (uint16_t)inl(0xCFC);
}

static void pci_config_write16(uint8_t bus, uint8_t device, uint8_t function, uint16_t offset, uint16_t value) {
    uint32_t address = (1 << 31) | (bus << 16) | (device << 11) | (function << 8) | (offset & ~1);
    outl(address, 0xCF8);
    outl(value, 0xCFC);
}

static void* map_memory_region(uint64_t base, size_t size) {
    int mem_fd = open("/dev/mem", O_RDWR);
    if (mem_fd < 0) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "Failed to open /dev/mem");
        return NULL;
    }
    
    // Align to page boundary
    uint64_t aligned_base = base & ~(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    size_t offset = base - aligned_base;
    size_t mapped_size = size + offset;
    
    void *mapped = mmap(NULL, mapped_size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, mem_fd, aligned_base);
    close(mem_fd);
    
    if (mapped == MAP_FAILED) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "Failed to map memory region 0x%lX", base);
        return NULL;
    }
    
    return (void*)((uint8_t*)mapped + offset);
}

static void unmap_memory_region(void *ptr, size_t size) {
    // Find the actual mapped base
    uintptr_t aligned_ptr = (uintptr_t)ptr & ~(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    size_t offset = (uintptr_t)ptr - aligned_ptr;
    size_t mapped_size = size + offset;
    munmap((void*)aligned_ptr, mapped_size);
}

static int check_i219_device(void) {
    log_msg("INFO", "Checking I219-V Ethernet controller...");
    
    uint32_t device_id = pci_config_read32(I219V_PCI_BUS, I219V_PCI_DEV, I219V_PCI_FUNC, 0x00);
    uint16_t vendor_id = device_id & 0xFFFF;
    uint16_t device = (device_id >> 16) & 0xFFFF;
    
    if (vendor_id != 0x8086) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "Not an Intel device (VID: 0x%04X)", vendor_id);
        return -1;
    }
    
    // Check for I219-V variants
    if (device != 0x15F && device != 0x15E && device != 0x15D && device != 0x15C && 
        device != 0x15B && device != 0x15A && device != 0x159 && device != 0x157) {
        log_msg("WARN", "Unknown I219 variant (DID: 0x%04X)", device);
    } else {
        log_msg("INFO", "Found I219-V Ethernet controller (VID:0x%04X DID:0x%04X)", vendor_id, device);
    }
    
    return 0;
}

static int acquire_eeprom_access(volatile uint32_t *i219_regs) {
    log_msg("INFO", "Acquiring EEPROM access...");
    
    // Check if EEPROM is present
    uint32_t eecd = i219_regs[I219_EECD/4];
    if (!(eecd & EECD_EE_PRES)) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "EEPROM not present");
        return -1;
    }
    
    // Request EEPROM access
    i219_regs[I219_EECD/4] = eecd | EECD_EE_REQ;
    
    // Wait for grant
    int timeout = 1000;
    while (timeout-- > 0) {
        eecd = i219_regs[I219_EECD/4];
        if (eecd & EECD_EE_GNT) {
            log_msg("INFO", "EEPROM access granted");
            return 0;
        }
        usleep(1000);
    }
    
    log_msg("ERROR", "Failed to acquire EEPROM access");
    return -1;
}

static void release_eeprom_access(volatile uint32_t *i219_regs) {
    log_msg("INFO", "Releasing EEPROM access...");
    
    uint32_t eecd = i219_regs[I219_EECD/4];
    i219_regs[I219_EECD/4] = eecd & ~EECD_EE_REQ;
}

static int read_eeprom_word(volatile uint32_t *i219_regs, uint16_t offset, uint16_t *data) {
    uint32_t eerd = (offset << 2) | EEPROM_READ_OPCODE;
    
    // Start read
    i219_regs[I219_EERD/4] = eerd;
    
    // Wait for completion
    int timeout = 1000;
    while (timeout-- > 0) {
        uint32_t eerd_val = i219_regs[I219_EERD/4];
        if (eerd_val & 0x1) {  // Done bit
            *data = (eerd_val >> 16) & 0xFFFF;
            return 0;
        }
        usleep(100);
    }
    
    log_msg("ERROR", "EEPROM read timeout at offset 0x%04X", offset);
    return -1;
}

static int write_eeprom_word(volatile uint32_t *i219_regs, uint16_t offset, uint16_t data) {
    log_msg("DEBUG", "Writing EEPROM word 0x%04X = 0x%04X", offset, data);
    
    uint32_t eecd = i219_regs[I219_EECD/4];
    
    // Enable write operations
    i219_regs[I219_EECD/4] = eecd | EECD_EE_FLASH_WR_EN;
    usleep(1000);
    
    // Write the word
    uint32_t eerd = (offset << 2) | EEPROM_WRITE_OPCODE | (data << 16);
    i219_regs[I219_EERD/4] = eerd;
    
    // Wait for write completion
    int timeout = 10000;  // Longer timeout for writes
    while (timeout-- > 0) {
        eecd = i219_regs[I219_EECD/4];
        if (!(eecd & EECD_EE_WI)) {  // Write done
            break;
        }
        usleep(100);
    }
    
    if (timeout == 0) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "EEPROM write timeout at offset 0x%04X", offset);
        return -1;
    }
    
    // Disable write operations
    eecd = i219_regs[I219_EECD/4];
    i219_regs[I219_EECD/4] = eecd & ~EECD_EE_FLASH_WR_EN;
    
    return 0;
}

static int backup_nvm(const char *backup_file) {
    log_msg("INFO", "Backing up NVM to %s...", backup_file);
    
    volatile uint32_t *i219_regs = (volatile uint32_t*)map_memory_region(I219V_BAR, 0x1000);
    if (!i219_regs) {
        return -1;
    }
    
    // Check management status
    uint32_t manc = i219_regs[I219_MANC/4];
    log_msg("INFO", "MANC Register: 0x%08X", manc);
    
    if (manc & 0x10000) {
        log_msg("WARN", "Ethernet is ME/AMT managed - may affect access");
    }
    
    // Acquire EEPROM access
    if (acquire_eeprom_access(i219_regs) < 0) {
        unmap_memory_region((void*)i219_regs, 0x1000);
        return -1;
    }
    
    // Read NVM
    uint16_t nvm_data[0x800];  // 4KB NVM
    int success = 1;
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 0x800; i++) {
        if (read_eeprom_word(i219_regs, i, &nvm_data[i]) < 0) {
            log_msg("ERROR", "Failed to read NVM word %d", i);
            success = 0;
            break;
        }
        
        if ((i % 256) == 0) {
            log_msg("INFO", "Read %d/2048 words", i);
        }
    }
    
    release_eeprom_access(i219_regs);
    unmap_memory_region((void*)i219_regs, 0x1000);
    
    if (!success) {
        return -1;
    }
    
    // Save backup
    FILE *fp = fopen(backup_file, "wb");
    if (!fp) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "Failed to create backup file: %s", backup_file);
        return -1;
    }
    
    size_t written = fwrite(nvm_data, 2, 0x800, fp);
    fclose(fp);
    
    if (written == 0x800) {
        log_msg("SUCCESS", "NVM backup completed (%zu words)", written);
        return 0;
    } else {
        log_msg("ERROR", "Incomplete backup: %zu/2048 words", written);
        return -1;
    }
}

static int restore_nvm(const char *nvm_file) {
    log_msg("INFO", "Restoring NVM from %s...", nvm_file);
    
    // Read NVM file
    FILE *fp = fopen(nvm_file, "rb");
    if (!fp) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "Failed to open NVM file: %s", nvm_file);
        return -1;
    }
    
    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);
    long file_size = ftell(fp);
    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);
    
    if (file_size > 0x1000) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "NVM file too large: %ld bytes (max 4KB)", file_size);
        fclose(fp);
        return -1;
    }
    
    uint16_t nvm_data[0x800];
    memset(nvm_data, 0xFF, sizeof(nvm_data));  // Default to 0xFF
    
    size_t words_read = fread(nvm_data, 2, file_size / 2, fp);
    fclose(fp);
    
    log_msg("INFO", "Read %zu words from NVM file", words_read);
    
    volatile uint32_t *i219_regs = (volatile uint32_t*)map_memory_region(I219V_BAR, 0x1000);
    if (!i219_regs) {
        return -1;
    }
    
    // Acquire EEPROM access
    if (acquire_eeprom_access(i219_regs) < 0) {
        unmap_memory_region((void*)i219_regs, 0x1000);
        return -1;
    }
    
    // Write NVM
    int success = 1;
    
    for (int i = 0; i < words_read; i++) {
        if (write_eeprom_word(i219_regs, i, nvm_data[i]) < 0) {
            log_msg("ERROR", "Failed to write NVM word %d", i);
            success = 0;
            break;
        }
        
        if ((i % 64) == 0) {
            log_msg("INFO", "Written %d/%zu words", i, words_read);
        }
    }
    
    release_eeprom_access(i219_regs);
    unmap_memory_region((void*)i219_regs, 0x1000);
    
    if (!success) {
        return -1;
    }
    
    log_msg("SUCCESS", "NVM restoration completed");
    
    // Reset Ethernet controller
    log_msg("INFO", "Resetting Ethernet controller...");
    
    uint16_t cmd = pci_config_read16(I219V_PCI_BUS, I219V_PCI_DEV, I219V_PCI_FUNC, 0x04);
    pci_config_write16(I219V_PCI_BUS, I219V_PCI_DEV, I219V_PCI_FUNC, 0x04, cmd & ~0x3);
    usleep(100000);
    pci_config_write16(I219V_PCI_BUS, I219V_PCI_DEV, I219V_PCI_FUNC, 0x04, cmd);
    
    log_msg("INFO", "Ethernet controller reset complete");
    
    return 0;
}

static int show_nvm_info(void) {
    log_msg("INFO", "Displaying NVM information...");
    
    volatile uint32_t *i219_regs = (volatile uint32_t*)map_memory_region(I219V_BAR, 0x1000);
    if (!i219_regs) {
        return -1;
    }
    
    // Show key registers
    uint32_t ctrl = i219_regs[I219_CTRL/4];
    uint32_t status = i219_regs[I219_STATUS/4];
    uint32_t eecd = i219_regs[I219_EECD/4];
    uint32_t manc = i219_regs[I219_MANC/4];
    uint32_t swsm = i219_regs[I219_SWSM/4];
    
    printf("I219-V Register Status:\n");
    printf("  CTRL:    0x%08X\n", ctrl);
    printf("  STATUS:  0x%08X\n", status);
    printf("  EECD:    0x%08X", eecd);
    if (eecd & EECD_EE_PRES) printf(" [EEPROM_PRESENT]");
    if (eecd & EECD_EE_GNT) printf(" [EEPROM_GRANT]");
    if (eecd & EECD_EE_REQ) printf(" [EEPROM_REQ]");
    printf("\n");
    printf("  MANC:    0x%08X", manc);
    if (manc & 0x10000) printf(" [ME_MANAGED]");
    printf("\n");
    printf("  SWSM:    0x%08X", swsm);
    if (swsm & 0x1) printf(" [SMBUS_LOCK]");
    printf("\n");
    
    // Read first few NVM words
    if (acquire_eeprom_access(i219_regs) == 0) {
        printf("\nNVM Contents (first 16 words):\n");
        
        for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
            uint16_t data;
            if (read_eeprom_word(i219_regs, i, &data) == 0) {
                printf("  [%04X]: %04X", i, data);
                if ((i % 4) == 3) printf("\n");
            }
        }
        
        release_eeprom_access(i219_regs);
    }
    
    unmap_memory_region((void*)i219_regs, 0x1000);
    
    return 0;
}

static void print_usage(const char *prog_name) {
    printf("DSMIL Ethernet NVM Restoration Tool\n");
    printf("==================================\n\n");
    printf("Usage: %s [options]\n\n", prog_name);
    printf("Options:\n");
    printf("  -b, --backup <file>   Backup NVM to file\n");
    printf("  -r, --restore <file>  Restore NVM from file\n");
    printf("  -i, --info            Show NVM information\n");
    printf("  -h, --help            Show this help\n");
    printf("\nExamples:\n");
    printf("  %s -b nvm_backup.bin   # Backup NVM\n", prog_name);
    printf("  %s -r nvm_backup.bin   # Restore NVM\n", prog_name);
    printf("  %s -i                  # Show NVM info\n", prog_name);
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    int opt;
    int action = 0;  // 0=none, 1=backup, 2=restore, 3=info
    char *file_arg = NULL;
    
    static struct option long_opts[] = {
        {"backup", required_argument, 0, 'b'},
        {"restore", required_argument, 0, 'r'},
        {"info", no_argument, 0, 'i'},
        {"help", no_argument, 0, 'h'},
        {0, 0, 0, 0}
    };
    
    if (geteuid() != 0) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "This program requires root privileges");
        printf("Run with: sudo %s\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }
    
    // Enable I/O port access
    if (ioperm(0xCF8, 8, 1) != 0) {
        log_msg("ERROR", "Failed to get I/O port permissions");
        return 1;
    }
    
    while ((opt = getopt_long(argc, argv, "b:r:ih", long_opts, NULL)) != -1) {
        switch (opt) {
            case 'b':
                action = 1;
                file_arg = optarg;
                break;
            case 'r':
                action = 2;
                file_arg = optarg;
                break;
            case 'i':
                action = 3;
                break;
            case 'h':
                print_usage(argv[0]);
                return 0;
            default:
                print_usage(argv[0]);
                return 1;
        }
    }
    
    // Check I219-V device
    if (check_i219_device() < 0) {
        return 1;
    }
    
    // Execute requested action
    switch (action) {
        case 1:  // backup
            if (!file_arg) {
                log_msg("ERROR", "Backup requires output file");
                break;
            }
            backup_nvm(file_arg);
            break;
        case 2:  // restore
            if (!file_arg) {
                log_msg("ERROR", "Restore requires input file");
                break;
            }
            restore_nvm(file_arg);
            break;
        case 3:  // info
            show_nvm_info();
            break;
        default:
            print_usage(argv[0]);
            break;
    }
    
    // Release I/O port permissions
    ioperm(0xCF8, 8, 0);
    
    return 0;
}

## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/ACPI DDST SSDT Firmware/acpi_tables/02_analysis_reports/README.md

# ACPI Tables Collection

## Overview
This directory contains Secondary System Description Tables (SSDTs) extracted from the system and related test documentation.

## Files
- **ssdt1.dat - ssdt21.dat**: Secondary System Description Tables
  - Various sizes ranging from 427 bytes to 39,734 bytes
  - Contains ACPI AML bytecode for system configuration
- **phat.dat**: Platform Hardware Address Table (1,872 bytes)
  - Hardware health monitoring and telemetry data
- **nhlt.dat**: Non-HDAudio Link Table (739 bytes)
  - Audio configuration for non-HDA audio devices
- **msdm.dat**: Microsoft Data Management (85 bytes)
  - Windows activation and licensing information
- **mcfg.dat**: Memory Configuration Table (60 bytes)
  - Memory controller configuration data
- **lpit.dat**: Low Power Idle Table (204 bytes)
  - Power management for low-power states
- **dsdt.dat**: Differentiated System Description Table (550,299 bytes)
  - Main system description table with device configuration
- **apic.dat**: APIC Table (604 bytes)
  - Multiprocessor configuration and interrupt routing
- **bgrt.dat**: Boot Graphics Resource Table (56 bytes)
  - Boot logo and graphics information
- **boot.dat**: Boot Table (40 bytes)
  - System boot configuration
- **dbg2.dat**: Debug Port 2 Table (84 bytes)
  - Debug port configuration
- **dbgp.dat**: Debug Port Table (52 bytes)
  - Legacy debug port information
- **dtpr.dat**: Device Tree Properties Table (136 bytes)
  - Device tree property data
- **facp.dat**: Fixed ACPI Description Table (276 bytes)
  - Fixed feature ACPI information
- **facs.dat**: Fixed ACPI Control Structure (64 bytes)
  - ACPI hardware register block
- **fpdt.dat**: Firmware Performance Data Table (52 bytes)
  - Boot performance metrics
- **hpet.dat**: High Precision Event Timer Table (56 bytes)
  - HPET configuration
- **tpm2.dat**: Trusted Platform Module 2.0 Table (76 bytes)
  - TPM 2.0 device configuration
- **TEST_SUMMARY.txt**: POLYGOTTEM Intel ML Enhancements deployment summary
  - 100% test coverage achieved (196/196 tests)
  - Intel ML integration and exotic ML enhancements verified

## Usage
These tables can be analyzed with:
- `iasl -d ssdt*.dat` - Decompile AML to ASL
- `acpidump` - ACPI table extraction utility
- `acpixtract` - Extract AML from ACPI tables

## Analysis Tools
- Intel ACPI Component Architecture (ACPICA)
- `acpiexec` - AML interpreter
- `acpisrc` - ACPI source conversion utility

## Hardware Context
These SSDTs are from a Dell Latitude 5450 JRTC1 with Meteor Lake-P processor (Core Ultra 7 165H).

## Security Notes
SSDTs may contain:
- Power management configurations
- Device enumeration data
- Hardware-specific optimizations
- Potential attack vectors for ACPI-based exploits

# RESEARCH AREA 210: 05_kernel_modules
**Path:** `intel-bug-bounty-report/ACPI DDST SSDT Firmware/acpi_tables/05_kernel_modules`


## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/ACPI DDST SSDT Firmware/acpi_tables/05_kernel_modules/README.md

# Kernel Modules

Hardware activation kernel modules for DSMIL covert edition features.

## I219-V ULP Force-Disable

### Overview
Forces I219-V Ethernet PHY out of Ultra Low Power (ULP) mode after NVM reflash.
e1000e driver fails with "Failed to disable ULP" / error -2 without this.

### Phased Approach
Controlled via `phase=N` module parameter:

| Phase | Action | Risk |
|-------|--------|------|
| 0 | Read-only diagnosis | None |
| 1 | MAC FEXTNVM7 ULP clear | Safe |
| 2 | + PHY ULP clear via MDIC | Safe (may timeout) |
| 3 | + Soft MAC reset (CTRL.RST) | Safe |
| 4 | + PHY reset (CTRL.PHY_RST) | Medium |
| 5 | + LANPHYPC toggle | **DANGEROUS** |

### Usage
```bash
# Phase 0: Diagnosis
sudo insmod i219_ulp_fix/i219_ulp_fix.ko
sudo dmesg | grep i219_ulp
sudo rmmod i219_ulp_fix

# Phase 3: Safe fix attempt
sudo insmod i219_ulp_fix/i219_ulp_fix.ko phase=3
sudo rmmod i219_ulp_fix && sudo modprobe e1000e
```

### Build
```bash
cd i219_ulp_fix/
make
```

## XCR0 Probe

### Overview
Probes XCR0 register state and CPUID features for AVX-512/AMX analysis.
Reports silicon fuse state and feature lock status.

### Features
- Reads XCR0 via xgetbv instruction
- Checks CPUID for AVX-512/AMX support
- Reports MSR feature control state
- Detects silicon fuse configuration

### Usage
```bash
sudo insmod xcr0_probe/xcr0_probe.ko
sudo dmesg | grep XCR0
```

### Build
```bash
cd xcr0_probe/
make
```

## Module Compatibility

- **Target Kernel**: 6.18.x (Debian 14)
- **API Changes**: Uses modern kernel APIs (no deprecated functions)
- **Safety**: All modules include error handling and cleanup

## Hardware Targets

| Module | Target | PCI Device | Physical Base |
|--------|--------|------------|---------------|
| i219_ulp_fix | I219-V Ethernet | 00:1f.6 | 0x7C100000 |
| xcr0_probe | CPU Features | N/A | MSRs via RDMSR |

## Security Notes

- All modules require root privileges
- MMIO access bypasses normal driver protections
- LANPHYPC toggle (phase 5) can cause PCH deadlock
- Modules log all actions for audit trails

---

# RESEARCH AREA 211: ucode_inject
**Path:** `intel-bug-bounty-report/ACPI DDST SSDT Firmware/acpi_tables/05_kernel_modules/ucode_inject`


## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/ACPI DDST SSDT Firmware/acpi_tables/05_kernel_modules/ucode_inject/README.md

# Red Key Microcode Injection via SPI Flash FIT Replacement

## Platform
- **CPU**: Intel Core Ultra 7 165H (Meteor Lake-P, CPUID 0x000A06A4)
- **Current microcode**: 0x24 (production, green key)
- **Target microcode**: 0x1C (engineering, red key)
- **Source**: `archive/06-aa-04_0x1c.bin` (136,192 bytes)

## Why Normal Loading Won't Work
1. **WRMSR 0x79 revision check**: CPU silicon refuses downgrade (0x1C < 0x24)
2. **FIT loads first**: BIOS FIT loads production 0x24 at reset, before any OS code
3. **Early initramfs**: Still uses WRMSR 0x79 — same silicon revision check
4. **`dis_ucode_ldr`**: Only disables Linux loader, FIT already loaded 0x24

## Strategy: SPI Flash FIT Replacement
Replace the production microcode in the BIOS SPI flash image with the red key
engineering microcode. On next cold boot, the FIT loads the red key microcode
FIRST — before any production code runs.

### Prerequisites
- `iomem=relaxed` on kernel command line (in GRUB defaults, needs normal boot)
- `lockdown=none` (in GRUB defaults)
- `flashrom` with internal programmer access
- DCI DEBUG_ACTIVE (confirmed: 0xF049B900) — indicates debug fuses accept red key

### DCI Debug State (Why Red Key Should Work)
```
DCI ctrl   = 0xF049B900  (JTAG+CSME_DEBUG+SVC_MODE_REQ+HEARTBEAT_ROUTE)
DCI status = 0x8CC38461  (DEBUG_ACTIVE + CONNECTED)
```
Production silicon does NOT have DEBUG_ACTIVE without debug fuses. The fact that
DCI shows debug-active strongly indicates this CPU will accept red-key-signed
microcode from the FIT.

## Execution Steps

### Step 1: Boot normally (not single mode)
Ensure `iomem=relaxed` and `lockdown=none` are active:
```bash
cat /proc/cmdline | grep iomem
```

### Step 2: Read current BIOS flash
```bash
sudo flashrom -p internal -r /tmp/bios_backup.bin
# KEEP THIS BACKUP SAFE — recovery depends on it
cp /tmp/bios_backup.bin /run/media/john/.../firmware/acpi_tables/05_kernel_modules/ucode_inject/bios_backup.bin
```

### Step 3: Analyze and inject
```bash
sudo python3 ucode_fit_inject.py \
    --bios /tmp/bios_backup.bin \
    --ucode ../../archive/06-aa-04_0x1c.bin \
    --output /tmp/bios_modified.bin
```

### Step 4: Flash modified image
```bash
sudo flashrom -p internal -w /tmp/bios_modified.bin
```

### Step 5: Cold reboot and verify
```bash
sudo reboot
# After reboot:
cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep microcode   # Should show 0x1c
# Check for AVX-512:
grep avx512 /proc/cpuinfo
# Check for AMX:
grep amx /proc/cpuinfo
```

## Recovery
If boot fails after flash:
1. Boot from USB with flashrom
2. Flash back `bios_backup.bin`
3. Or: BIOS recovery via Dell BIOS recovery key (Ctrl+Esc at power-on)

## Microcode Header Analysis
```
Header version:    1
Update revision:   0x1C (28) — engineering
Date:              2024-01-03
CPUID signature:   0x000A06A4 (Family 6, Model 0xAA, Step 4)
Platform flags:    0xE6 (bits 1,2,5,6,7 — multi-platform)
Data size:         136,144 bytes
Total size:        136,192 bytes
RSA signature:     Red key (engineering debug key)
```

```
│   └── utilities/                # General utilities
│
├── systems/                       # System-specific tools
│   ├── mcm1000/                   # MCM-1000 driver & tools
│   ├── gna/                       # GNA driver
│   ├── tpm/                       # TPM analysis & testing
│   ├── mei-amt/                   # MEI/AMT tools
│   └── clearance/                # Clearance & authorization tools
│
├── archives/                      # Archived data
│   ├── apex_db/                   # From APEX DB/
│   └── data/                      # From DATA/ + data/
│
├── recovery/                      # Recovery tools
│   ├── mtl_recovery_suite/        # From MTL-RECOVERY-SUITE/
│   └── unlock/                    # From unlock/
│
├── ai/                            # AI tools
├── assets/                        # Assets
├── core20_avx512/                 # Core20 AVX512 tools
├── battlematrix/                  # From BATTLEMATRIX_TOOLS/
└── Makefile                       # Build system
```

## Quick Start

### Documentation
- Hardware guides: `docs/hardware_guides/`
- Mission reports: `docs/mission_reports/`
- Integration playbooks: `docs/integration_playbooks/`

### Reports
- Analysis reports: `reports/analysis_reports/`
- Comprehensive analysis: `reports/comprehensive_analysis/`
- Test results: `reports/test_results/`

### Tooling
- Scripts: `tooling/scripts/`
- Scanners: `tooling/scanners/`
- Drivers: `tooling/drivers/`

### System Tools
- MCM-1000: `systems/mcm1000/`
- TPM: `systems/tpm/`
- GNA: `systems/gna/`
- Clearance: `systems/clearance/`

## Key Features

- **Clear separation of concerns** - docs, reports, tooling, systems
- **Consistent naming conventions** - lowercase with underscores
- **Logical grouping by function** - related tools together
- **Scalable structure** - easy to add new components

## Integration Notes

### Tools Integration
- Canary token tools integrated from `/tools/`
- GbE manipulation tools integrated from `/tools/`
- Monitoring tools (titan_shadow_monitor, thermal_hud) integrated from `/tools/`

### TPM Suite
- Merged from `scripts/tpm/` into `systems/tpm/`
- Consolidated with existing `TPM_ANALYSIS/`
- Includes algorithm testing, bypass techniques, Intel exploitation

### Clearance Tools
- Integrated from `scripts/clearence/` into `systems/clearance/`
- Includes layer activation, vault checking, token mapping

## Build System

The `Makefile` provides targets for building and testing tools:

```bash
make all          # Build all tools
make install      # Install to /opt/dsmil/tools
make test         # Run tests
make clean        # Clean build artifacts
```

## Documentation

For detailed documentation on specific components:
- TPM Suite: `systems/tpm/README_TPM_SCRIPTS.md`
- Intel Exploitation: `systems/tpm/README_INTEL_EXPLOITATION.md`
- TPM Integration: `systems/tpm/README_TPM_INTEGRATION.md`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                         APEX-HUD v2.0                                        ║
║           IRONCLAD TITAN V6.0 - Sovereign Telemetry Dashboard               ║
║                                                                              ║
║  Platform: JRTC1-MILSPEC (Intel Meteor Lake-P)                              ║
║  Features: 13 PMT Endpoints | NPU Strategic Path | Energy Metering          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
"""

import os
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime

# ANSI Color Codes
class C:
    R = '\033[1;31m'      # Red
    G = '\033[1;32m'      # Green
    Y = '\033[1;33m'      # Yellow
    B = '\033[1;34m'      # Blue
    C = '\033[1;36m'      # Cyan
    M = '\033[1;35m'      # Magenta
    W = '\033[1;37m'      # White
    GR = '\033[0;37m'     # Gray
    NC = '\033[0m'        # No Color
    BLD = '\033[1m'       # Bold
    DIM = '\033[2m'       # Dim
    BLK = '\033[5m'       # Blink
    INV = '\033[7m'       # Inverse

# Configuration
MCM_SYSFS = "/sys/class/mcm1000/mcm0"
REFRESH_RATE = 0.5  # 500ms refresh

# Telemetry Device Map
TELEM_DEVICES = {
    1:  {"name": "AMX/PMT Control",    "offset": "0x744",  "function": "Feature Unlock"},
    2:  {"name": "CPU Core Metrics",   "offset": "0x1400", "function": "P-Core Telemetry"},
    3:  {"name": "Uncore/Ring Bus",    "offset": "0x1800", "function": "Interconnect"},
    4:  {"name": "Power Metering",     "offset": "0x2000", "function": "Energy Monitor"},
    5:  {"name": "Thermal Sentinel",   "offset": "0x3200", "function": "Governor Link"},
    6:  {"name": "IO Subsystem",       "offset": "0x3004", "function": "Peripheral Bus"},
    7:  {"name": "PCIe/Thunderbolt",   "offset": "0x3008", "function": "External Links"},
    8:  {"name": "Display/Media",      "offset": "0x300C", "function": "Graphics Path"},
    9:  {"name": "NPU Strategic",      "offset": "0x3344", "function": "APEX Engine"},
    10: {"name": "Memory Integrity",   "offset": "0x104",  "function": "NC3 Guard"},
    11: {"name": "GT/Graphics",        "offset": "0x3010", "function": "iGPU Metrics"},
    12: {"name": "SoC Tile",           "offset": "0x3014", "function": "LPE Cores"},
    13: {"name": "Compute Tile",       "offset": "0x3018", "function": "P-Core Tile"},
}


class ApexHUD:
    def __init__(self):
        self.running = True
        self.frame_count = 0
        self.start_time = time.time()
        
    def read_sysfs(self, attr, default="N/A"):
        """Read a sysfs attribute"""
        path = f"{MCM_SYSFS}/{attr}"
        try:
            with open(path, 'r') as f:
                return f.read().strip()
        except:
            return default
    
    def read_int(self, attr, default=0):
        """Read integer sysfs attribute"""
        try:
            return int(self.read_sysfs(attr, str(default)))
        except:
            return default
    
    def clear(self):
        """Clear terminal"""
        os.system('clear')
    
    def bar(self, value, max_val, width=20, fill_char="█", empty_char="░"):
        """Generate a progress bar"""
        if max_val == 0:
            filled = 0
        else:
            filled = min(int(value * width / max_val), width)
        empty = width - filled
        return fill_char * filled + empty_char * empty
    
    def color_temp(self, temp):
        """Color based on temperature"""
        if temp >= 100:
            return C.R
        elif temp >= 80:
            return C.Y
        else:
            return C.G
    
    def color_util(self, util):
        """Color based on utilization"""
        if util >= 90:
            return C.R
        elif util >= 70:
            return C.Y
        else:
            return C.G
    
    def sovereign_status(self, unlocked):
        """Return sovereign status indicator"""
        if unlocked:
            return f"{C.G}◆ SOVEREIGN{C.NC}"
        else:
            return f"{C.R}◇ RESTRICTED{C.NC}"
    
    def print_header(self):
        """Print HUD header"""
        now = datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S")
        uptime = int(time.time() - self.start_time)
        
        print(f"{C.C}╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}  {C.W}APEX-HUD v2.0{C.NC} │ {C.GR}IRONCLAD TITAN V6.0{C.NC} │ {C.Y}{now}{C.NC} │ {C.GR}Uptime: {uptime}s{C.NC}        {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣{C.NC}")
    
    def print_sovereign_block(self):
        """Print sovereign status block"""
        unlocked = self.read_sysfs("unlock_silicon") == "1"
        clock_sync = self.read_sysfs("vsec_clock_sync") == "1"
        me_squelch = self.read_sysfs("vsec_me_squelch") == "1"
        rail_boost = self.read_int("vsec_rail_boost")
        sram_tunnel = self.read_sysfs("sram_tunnel") == "1"
        
        status = self.sovereign_status(unlocked)
        
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC} {C.W}SOVEREIGN STATUS{C.NC}                                                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Silicon: {status:<30}                               {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        
        # Feature indicators
        features = []
        if clock_sync:
            features.append(f"{C.G}SYNC:LOCKED{C.NC}")
        else:
            features.append(f"{C.GR}SYNC:FREE{C.NC}")
        
        if me_squelch:
            features.append(f"{C.G}ME:SQUELCHED{C.NC}")
        else:
            features.append(f"{C.Y}ME:ACTIVE{C.NC}")
        
        if rail_boost > 0:
            features.append(f"{C.Y}RAIL:+{rail_boost}%{C.NC}")
        else:
            features.append(f"{C.GR}RAIL:NOM{C.NC}")
        
        if sram_tunnel:
            features.append(f"{C.G}TUNNEL:ON{C.NC}")
        else:
            features.append(f"{C.GR}TUNNEL:OFF{C.NC}")
        
        feat_str = " │ ".join(features)
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   {feat_str:<72} {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}                                                                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
    
    def print_npu_block(self):
        """Print NPU Strategic Path block"""
        npu_freq = self.read_int("npu_freq")
        npu_util = self.read_int("npu_util")
        npu_tops = self.read_int("npu_tops")
        
        # Calculate display values
        freq_bar = self.bar(npu_freq, 2000, 15)  # Assume 2GHz max
        util_bar = self.bar(npu_util, 100, 15)
        tops_bar = self.bar(npu_tops, 1419, 15)   # 1,419 TOPS max
        
        util_color = self.color_util(npu_util)
        
        print(f"{C.C}╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC} {C.W}NPU STRATEGIC PATH{C.NC} (telem9 @ 0x3344)                                        {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Frequency:   {C.B}{freq_bar}{C.NC} {npu_freq:>5} MHz                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Utilization: {util_color}{util_bar}{C.NC} {npu_util:>5} %                               {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   TOPS:        {C.M}{tops_bar}{C.NC} {npu_tops:>5} / 1,419                          {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}                                                                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
    
    def print_energy_block(self):
        """Print energy consumption block"""
        power_mw = self.read_int("power_mw")
        power_limit = self.read_int("power_limit")
        if power_limit == 0:
            power_limit = 65  # Default MILSPEC
        
        power_w = power_mw / 1000.0
        power_bar = self.bar(power_w, power_limit, 20)
        
        if power_w >= power_limit * 0.9:
            power_color = C.R
        elif power_w >= power_limit * 0.7:
            power_color = C.Y
        else:
            power_color = C.G
        
        print(f"{C.C}╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC} {C.W}ENERGY CONSUMPTION{C.NC} (telem4 @ 0x2000)                                        {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Power Draw:  {power_color}{power_bar}{C.NC} {power_w:>6.1f}W / {power_limit}W             {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        
        # Efficiency estimate
        if npu_tops := self.read_int("npu_tops"):
            if power_w > 0:
                efficiency = npu_tops / power_w
                print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Efficiency:  {C.G}{efficiency:>6.1f} TOPS/W{C.NC}                                           {C.C}║{C.NC}")
            else:
                print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Efficiency:  {C.GR}N/A{C.NC}                                                        {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        else:
            print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Efficiency:  {C.GR}IDLE{C.NC}                                                       {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}                                                                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
    
    def print_thermal_block(self):
        """Print thermal block"""
        soc_temp = self.read_int("soc_temp")
        peak_temp = self.read_int("soc_temp_peak", soc_temp)
        
        temp_bar = self.bar(soc_temp, 110, 20)
        temp_color = self.color_temp(soc_temp)
        
        print(f"{C.C}╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC} {C.W}THERMAL SENTINEL{C.NC} (telem5 @ 0x3200)                                          {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   SoC Temp:    {temp_color}{temp_bar}{C.NC} {soc_temp:>3}°C / 110°C T-MAX         {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        
        # Thermal zones
        turbo = self.read_sysfs("turbo_fan", "0") == "1"
        squelch = self.read_sysfs("emergency_squelch", "0") == "1"
        
        if squelch:
            status = f"{C.R}█ EMERGENCY SQUELCH{C.NC}"
        elif turbo:
            status = f"{C.Y}█ TURBO FAN ACTIVE{C.NC}"
        elif soc_temp >= 80:
            status = f"{C.Y}█ ELEVATED{C.NC}"
        else:
            status = f"{C.G}█ NOMINAL{C.NC}"
        
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Status:      {status:<50}           {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}                                                                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
    
    def print_memory_block(self):
        """Print memory integrity block"""
        mem_bw = self.read_int("mem_bw")
        nc3_breach = self.read_int("nc3_breach")
        
        bw_bar = self.bar(mem_bw, 100000, 15)  # 100GB/s max
        
        if nc3_breach > 0:
            breach_status = f"{C.R}⚠ {nc3_breach} BREACHES{C.NC}"
        else:
            breach_status = f"{C.G}✓ SECURE{C.NC}"
        
        print(f"{C.C}╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC} {C.W}MEMORY INTEGRITY{C.NC} (telem10 @ 0x104)                                          {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Bandwidth:   {C.B}{bw_bar}{C.NC} {mem_bw:>6} MB/s                          {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   NC3 Vault:   {breach_status:<50}            {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}                                                                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
    
    def print_telem_grid(self):
        """Print 13 telemetry device status grid"""
        print(f"{C.C}╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC} {C.W}TELEMETRY DEVICES{C.NC} (13 PMT Endpoints)                                         {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}                                                                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        
        # Read active status from various indicators
        silicon_unlocked = self.read_sysfs("unlock_silicon") == "1"
        heartbeat = self.read_sysfs("heartbeat_running") == "1"
        
        # Device status grid (3 columns)
        for row in range(5):
            line = "   "
            for col in range(3):
                idx = row * 3 + col + 1
                if idx > 13:
                    line += "                        "
                    continue
                    
                dev = TELEM_DEVICES[idx]
                
                # Determine status based on device type
                if idx == 1:  # AMX/PMT
                    active = silicon_unlocked
                elif idx == 5:  # Thermal
                    active = True  # Always active
                elif idx == 9:  # NPU
                    active = self.read_int("npu_freq") > 0
                elif idx == 10:  # Memory
                    active = True  # Always monitoring
                elif idx == 12:  # SoC Tile
                    active = heartbeat
                else:
                    active = silicon_unlocked or heartbeat
                
                if active:
                    status = f"{C.G}●{C.NC}"
                else:
                    status = f"{C.GR}○{C.NC}"
                
                name = dev["name"][:14].ljust(14)
                line += f"{status} {C.GR}{idx:02d}{C.NC} {name}   "
            
            print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}{line}      {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}                                                                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
    
    def print_network_block(self):
        """Print network identity block"""
        gbe_status = self.read_sysfs("gbe_status", "UNKNOWN")
        gbe_injected = self.read_sysfs("gbe_injected", "0") == "1"
        
        if gbe_injected:
            status = f"{C.G}█ SHADOW-LATCHED{C.NC}"
        elif gbe_status == "READY":
            status = f"{C.Y}█ READY FOR INJECTION{C.NC}"
        else:
            status = f"{C.R}█ {gbe_status}{C.NC}"
        
        print(f"{C.C}╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC} {C.W}NETWORK IDENTITY{C.NC} (GBE Port 0xAF)                                            {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}   Shadow RAM:  {status:<50}           {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC}                                                                              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
    
    def print_footer(self):
        """Print HUD footer"""
        print(f"{C.C}╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}║{C.NC} {C.GR}[U] Unlock Silicon | [S] Sync Clock | [M] ME Squelch | [Q] Quit{C.NC}              {C.C}║{C.NC}")
        print(f"{C.C}╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝{C.NC}")
    
    def write_sysfs(self, attr, value):
        """Write to sysfs attribute"""
        path = f"{MCM_SYSFS}/{attr}"
        try:
            with open(path, 'w') as f:
                f.write(str(value))
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"{C.R}Failed to write {attr}: {e}{C.NC}")
            return False
    
    def display(self):
        """Render full HUD"""
        self.clear()
        self.print_header()
        self.print_sovereign_block()
        self.print_npu_block()
        self.print_energy_block()
        self.print_thermal_block()
        self.print_memory_block()
        self.print_telem_grid()
        self.print_network_block()
        self.print_footer()
        self.frame_count += 1
    
    def run(self):
        """Main HUD loop"""
        import select
        import tty
        import termios
        
        old_settings = termios.tcgetattr(sys.stdin)
        
        try:
            tty.setcbreak(sys.stdin.fileno())
            
            while self.running:
                self.display()
                
                # Check for input with timeout
                if select.select([sys.stdin], [], [], REFRESH_RATE)[0]:
                    key = sys.stdin.read(1).lower()
                    
                    if key == 'q':
                        self.running = False
                    elif key == 'u':
                        print(f"\n{C.Y}Unlocking silicon...{C.NC}")
                        self.write_sysfs("unlock_silicon", "1")
                        time.sleep(1)
                    elif key == 's':
                        current = self.read_sysfs("vsec_clock_sync") == "1"
                        self.write_sysfs("vsec_clock_sync", "0" if current else "1")
                    elif key == 'm':
                        current = self.read_sysfs("vsec_me_squelch") == "1"
                        self.write_sysfs("vsec_me_squelch", "0" if current else "1")
        
        finally:
            termios.tcsetattr(sys.stdin, termios.TCSADRAIN, old_settings)
        
        print(f"\n{C.C}APEX-HUD v2.0 terminated.{C.NC}")


def main():
    # Check for root
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print(f"{C.R}ERROR: This script requires root privileges.{C.NC}")
        print(f"Run with: sudo python3 {sys.argv[0]}")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Check for MCM driver
    if not os.path.exists(MCM_SYSFS):
        print(f"{C.R}ERROR: IRONCLAD TITAN driver not loaded.{C.NC}")
        print(f"Load with: sudo insmod mcm1000.ko")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    print(f"{C.C}Starting APEX-HUD v2.0...{C.NC}")
    time.sleep(0.5)
    
    hud = ApexHUD()
    hud.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
