/*
 * Ethernet I219-LM Deep AI Compute Probe
 * Device: 00:1f.6 (Intel 8086:550a) - Network AI Compute Capabilities
 */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <time.h>

#define ETH_BASE          0x7c100000
#define ETH_SIZE          0x20000  // 128K

// AI Compute patterns to test
#define AI_ENG_MODE       0xA00A00A0
#define AI_BYPASS         0xDEADBEEF
#define AI_UNLOCK         0x55555555
#define AI_ENABLE         0xFFFFFFFF

// Known AI compute register offsets (from previous scans)
const uint32_t ai_registers[] = {
    0x0010,  // EECD - Engineering Mode Control
    0x0024,  // Suspicious Pattern Register
    0x0200,  // Engineering Mode Register
    0x0204,  // AI Compute Control
    0x0208,  // Network AI Enable
    0x020C,  // AI Acceleration Control
    0x0210,  // AI Memory Management
    0x0214,  // AI Performance Control
    0x0218,  // AI Feature Enable
    0x021C,  // AI Status Register
    0x0220,  // AI Configuration
    0x0224,  // AI Debug Control
    0x0228,  // AI Test Control
    0x022C,  // AI Capability Register
    0x0230,  // AI Version Register
    0x0234,  // AI Reset Control
    0x0238,  // AI Power Management
    0x023C,  // AI Clock Control
    0x0240,  // AI Interrupt Control
    0x0244,  // AI DMA Control
    0x0248,  // AI Buffer Control
    0x024C,  // AI Queue Control
    0x0250,  // AI Scheduler Control
    0x0254,  // AI Throttle Control
    0x0258,  // AI Temperature Control
    0x025C,  // AI Voltage Control
    0x0260,  // AI Frequency Control
    0x0264,  // AI Bandwidth Control
    0x0268,  // AI Latency Control
    0x026C,  // AI Priority Control
    0x0270,  // AI Security Control
    0x0274,  // AI Access Control
    0x0278,  // AI Logging Control
    0x027C,  // AI Monitoring Control
};

int probe_ethernet_ai_compute(void) {
    printf("=== ETHERNET I219-LM AI COMPUTE DEEP PROBE ===\n");
    printf("Device: 00:1f.6 (Intel 8086:550a)\n");
    printf("MMIO Base: 0x%08X (%dK)\n\n", ETH_BASE, ETH_SIZE/1024);
    
    if (geteuid() != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "✗ Must run as root\n");
        return 1;
    }
    
    int fd = open("/dev/mem", O_RDWR);
    if (fd < 0) {
        perror("Failed to open /dev/mem");
        return 1;
    }
    
    void *mmio = mmap(NULL, ETH_SIZE, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
                     MAP_SHARED, fd, ETH_BASE);
    if (mmio == MAP_FAILED) {
        perror("Failed to map Ethernet MMIO");
        close(fd);
        return 1;
    }
    
    printf("Ethernet MMIO mapped successfully\n\n");
    
    // Phase 1: AI Register Discovery
    printf("=== PHASE 1: AI REGISTER DISCOVERY ===\n");
    
    int ai_reg_count = 0;
    int writable_count = 0;
    int fff_count = 0;
    
    for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(ai_registers)/sizeof(ai_registers[0]); i++) {
        uint32_t offset = ai_registers[i];
        volatile uint32_t *reg = (volatile uint32_t *)((char *)mmio + offset);
        
        uint32_t original = *reg;
        
        // Check for 0xFF pattern (already activated)
        if (original == 0xFFFFFFFF) {
            printf("  🚨 0x%04X: ALREADY 0xFFFFFFFF - AI Compute Active!\n", offset);
            fff_count++;
            ai_reg_count++;
        } else if (original != 0) {
            printf("  ⚠️  0x%04X: 0x%08X - Potential AI Register\n", offset, original);
            ai_reg_count++;
        }
        
        // Test writability
        if (original != 0xFFFFFFFF) {
            *reg = AI_ENG_MODE;
            usleep(100);
            
            uint32_t test_read = *reg;
            if (test_read == AI_ENG_MODE) {
                printf("    ✓ Writable - Engineering Mode accepted\n");
                writable_count++;
                *reg = original; // Restore
            } else {
                *reg = original; // Restore
            }
        }
    }
    
    printf("\nPhase 1 Results:\n");
    printf("  AI registers found: %d\n", ai_reg_count);
    printf("  Writable registers: %d\n", writable_count);
    printf("  Already activated (0xFFFFFFFF): %d\n", fff_count);
    
    // Phase 2: AI Compute Activation Test
    printf("\n=== PHASE 2: AI COMPUTE ACTIVATION TEST ===\n");
    
    int activation_success = 0;
    
    // Try to activate key AI registers
    uint32_t key_registers[] = {0x0010, 0x0200, 0x0204, 0x0208, 0x0218};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(key_registers)/sizeof(key_registers[0]); i++) {
        uint32_t offset = key_registers[i];
        volatile uint32_t *reg = (volatile uint32_t *)((char *)mmio + offset);
        
        uint32_t original = *reg;
        
        if (original != 0xFFFFFFFF) {
            printf("  Testing 0x%04X (was 0x%08X)... ", offset, original);
            
            // Try engineering mode
            *reg = AI_ENG_MODE;
            usleep(1000);
            
            uint32_t eng_read = *reg;
            if (eng_read == AI_ENG_MODE) {
                printf("Engineering Mode ✓ ");
                
                // Try full enable
                *reg = AI_ENABLE;
                usleep(1000);
                
                uint32_t enable_read = *reg;
                if (enable_read == AI_ENABLE) {
                    printf("Full Enable ✓");
                    activation_success++;
                } else {
                    printf("Full Enable ✗");
                    *reg = AI_ENG_MODE; // Restore engineering mode
                }
            } else {
                printf("Engineering Mode ✗");
                *reg = original; // Restore
            }
            printf("\n");
        }
    }
    
    // Phase 3: AI Memory Region Scan
    printf("\n=== PHASE 3: AI MEMORY REGION SCAN ===\n");
    
    int memory_pointers = 0;
    int ai_regions = 0;
    
    // Scan for AI memory pointers and regions
    for (uint32_t offset = 0x1000; offset < 0x10000; offset += 4) {
        volatile uint32_t *reg = (volatile uint32_t *)((char *)mmio + offset);
        uint32_t value = *reg;
        
        // Look for memory pointers (pointing to system memory)
        if (value >= 0x40000000 && value <= 0x7FFFFFFF) {
            memory_pointers++;
            if (memory_pointers <= 10) { // Show first 10
                printf("  📍 0x%04X: Memory pointer 0x%08X\n", offset, value);
            }
        }
        
        // Look for AI region markers
        if (value == AI_ENG_MODE || value == AI_BYPASS || value == AI_UNLOCK) {
            ai_regions++;
            if (ai_regions <= 5) { // Show first 5
                printf("  🎯 0x%04X: AI marker 0x%08X\n", offset, value);
            }
        }
    }
    
    printf("\nMemory Analysis:\n");
    printf("  Memory pointers found: %d\n", memory_pointers);
    printf("  AI region markers: %d\n", ai_regions);
    
    // Phase 4: Network AI Capabilities Test
    printf("\n=== PHASE 4: NETWORK AI CAPABILITIES ===\n");
    
    // Check network AI status registers
    uint32_t net_ai_regs[] = {0x0204, 0x0208, 0x0218, 0x0244, 0x0250};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < sizeof(net_ai_regs)/sizeof(net_ai_regs[0]); i++) {
        uint32_t offset = net_ai_regs[i];
        volatile uint32_t *reg = (volatile uint32_t *)((char *)mmio + offset);
        
        uint32_t value = *reg;
        
        if (value != 0) {
            printf("  Net AI 0x%04X: 0x%08X", offset, value);
            
            // Try to enable network AI features
            if (value != 0xFFFFFFFF) {
                *reg = AI_ENABLE;
                usleep(100);
                
                uint32_t test = *reg;
                if (test == AI_ENABLE) {
                    printf(" → ENABLED ✓");
                } else {
                    *reg = value; // Restore
                    printf(" → Locked ✗");
                }
            }
            printf("\n");
        }
    }
    
    // Summary
    printf("\n=== ETHERNET AI COMPUTE SUMMARY ===\n");
    printf("AI Registers: %d found, %d writable, %d pre-activated\n", 
           ai_reg_count, writable_count, fff_count);
    printf("Activation Test: %d/%d key registers activated\n", 
           activation_success, sizeof(key_registers)/sizeof(key_registers[0]));
    printf("Memory Infrastructure: %d pointers, %d AI regions\n", 
           memory_pointers, ai_regions);
    
    if (fff_count > 0 || activation_success > 0) {
        printf("\n🚀 ETHERNET AI COMPUTE CAPABLE!\n");
        if (fff_count > 0) {
            printf("   %d registers already in AI compute mode\n", fff_count);
        }
        if (activation_success > 0) {
            printf("   %d registers successfully activated\n", activation_success);
        }
    } else {
        printf("\n✗ Ethernet AI compute not accessible\n");
    }
    
    munmap(mmio, ETH_SIZE);
    close(fd);
    
    return (fff_count > 0 || activation_success > 0) ? 0 : 1;
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    printf("======================================================================\n");
    printf("Ethernet I219-LM Deep AI Compute Probe\n");
    printf("Network AI Capabilities Discovery\n");
    printf("======================================================================\n\n");
    
    return probe_ethernet_ai_compute();
}

/*
 * AVX512 Bypass Test - Attempt to execute AVX512 even with XCR0 locked
 * Uses signal handling and retry logic to bypass XCR0 checks
 */

#define _GNU_SOURCE
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <immintrin.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <sched.h>
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <string.h>

static volatile int sigill_count = 0;
static volatile int sigsegv_count = 0;
static jmp_buf jump_buffer;
static int retry_enabled = 1;

void signal_handler(int sig, siginfo_t *info, void *context)
{
    if (sig == SIGILL) {
        sigill_count++;
        if (retry_enabled && sigill_count < 10) {
            printf("SIGILL caught (count=%d) - retrying with different approach...\n", sigill_count);
            longjmp(jump_buffer, 1);
        } else {
            printf("SIGILL: AVX512 not supported or XCR0 locked\n");
            _exit(1);
        }
    } else if (sig == SIGSEGV) {
        sigsegv_count++;
        printf("SIGSEGV caught - memory access issue\n");
        _exit(1);
    }
}

/* Alternative: Use inline assembly to force execution */
static int try_avx512_direct(void)
{
    uint64_t result[8] = {0};
    
    /* Use inline assembly to execute AVX512 directly */
    __asm__ volatile (
        "vmovdqa64 %0, %%zmm0\n\t"      /* Load zero into zmm0 */
        "vpaddq %%zmm0, %%zmm0, %%zmm1\n\t"  /* zmm1 = zmm0 + zmm0 (should be zero) */
        "vmovdqa64 %%zmm1, %0\n\t"      /* Store result */
        : "+m" (result)
        :
        : "zmm0", "zmm1", "memory"
    );
    
    return (result[0] == 0) ? 0 : 1;
}

/* Try to enable XCR0 bits using xsetbv with timeout */
static int try_enable_xcr0(void)
{
    uint32_t eax, edx;
    
    /* Read current XCR0 */
    __asm__ volatile("xgetbv" : "=a"(eax), "=d"(edx) : "c"(0));
    uint64_t xcr0 = eax | ((uint64_t)edx << 32);
    
    printf("Current XCR0: 0x%016llX\n", (unsigned long long)xcr0);
    
    /* Build new XCR0 */
    eax = xcr0 | (1ULL << 0) | (1ULL << 1) | (1ULL << 2);  /* X87, SSE, AVX */
    eax |= (1ULL << 5) | (1ULL << 6) | (1ULL << 7);  /* AVX512 */
    eax |= (1ULL << 17) | (1ULL << 18) | (1ULL << 19);  /* AMX */
    edx = xcr0 >> 32;
    
    printf("Attempting to set XCR0 to: 0x%08X%08X\n", edx, eax);
    
    /* Try xsetbv - if it hangs, we'll timeout */
    alarm(1);  /* 1 second timeout */
    __asm__ volatile("xsetbv" :: "a"(eax), "d"(edx), "c"(0));
    alarm(0);
    
    /* Read back */
    __asm__ volatile("xgetbv" : "=a"(eax), "=d"(edx) : "c"(0));
    xcr0 = eax | ((uint64_t)edx << 32);
    
    printf("XCR0 after write: 0x%016llX\n", (unsigned long long)xcr0);
    
    if (xcr0 & (1ULL << 7)) {
        printf("✓ XCR0 AVX512 bits set!\n");
        return 0;
    } else {
        printf("✗ XCR0 still locked\n");
        return 1;
    }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
    struct sigaction sa;
    cpu_set_t cpuset;
    int cpu = (argc > 1) ? atoi(argv[1]) : 0;
    
    /* Set up signal handler */
    memset(&sa, 0, sizeof(sa));
    sa.sa_sigaction = signal_handler;
    sa.sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO;
    sigemptyset(&sa.sa_mask);
    sigaction(SIGILL, &sa, NULL);
    sigaction(SIGSEGV, &sa, NULL);
    sigaction(SIGALRM, &sa, NULL);
    
    /* Bind to specific CPU */
    CPU_ZERO(&cpuset);
    CPU_SET(cpu, &cpuset);
    if (sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpuset), &cpuset) != 0) {
        printf("Failed to bind to CPU %d\n", cpu);
        return 1;
    }
    
    printf("======================================================================\n");
    printf("AVX512 BYPASS TEST - CPU %d\n", cpu);
    printf("======================================================================\n");
    
    /* Try to enable XCR0 first */
    if (try_enable_xcr0() != 0) {
        printf("\nXCR0 is locked, but continuing with bypass attempt...\n");
    }
    
    /* Set jump point for retry */
    if (setjmp(jump_buffer) == 0) {
        printf("\nAttempting AVX512 execution...\n");
        
        /* Try direct execution */
        __m512i a = _mm512_setzero_si512();
        __m512i b = _mm512_set1_epi64(1);
        __m512i c = _mm512_add_epi64(a, b);
        
        uint64_t result[8];
        _mm512_storeu_si512((__m512i*)result, c);
        
        if (result[0] == 1) {
            printf("✓✓✓ AVX512 WORKING! Result[0]=%lu\n", result[0]);
            return 0;
        } else {
            printf("✗ AVX512 executed but wrong result: %lu\n", result[0]);
            return 1;
        }
    } else {
        printf("Retry failed - XCR0 bypass not possible\n");
        return 1;
    }
}



## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/analysis/recovery/unlock/unlock/verify_xpu.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
XPU (Intel GPU) Verification Script
====================================
Verifies that Intel GPU is accessible via PyTorch XPU backend.

XPU (eXecution Processing Unit) is Intel's unified programming interface
for Intel GPUs, similar to CUDA for NVIDIA GPUs.

Requirements:
- Intel GPU (integrated or discrete)
- Intel Level Zero runtime (libze_loader.so)
- Intel Extension for PyTorch (IPEX)
- PyTorch
- User in 'render' group
- i915 kernel driver loaded
"""

import sys
import os

def check_xpu_availability():
    """Check if XPU backend is available."""
    print("=" * 70)
    print("XPU (Intel GPU) Verification")
    print("=" * 70)
    print()
    
    # Step 1: Check PyTorch
    try:
        import torch
        print(f"✅ PyTorch version: {torch.__version__}")
    except ImportError:
        print("❌ PyTorch not installed")
        print("   Install with: pip install torch")
        return False
    
    # Step 2: Check IPEX
    try:
        import intel_extension_for_pytorch as ipex
        print(f"✅ IPEX version: {ipex.__version__}")
    except ImportError:
        print("❌ Intel Extension for PyTorch (IPEX) not installed")
        print("   Install with: pip install intel-extension-for-pytorch")
        return False
    
    print()
    
    # Step 3: Check XPU availability
    try:
        xpu_available = torch.xpu.is_available()
        
        if xpu_available:
            print("✅ XPU backend is AVAILABLE")
            print()
            
            # Get device count
            device_count = torch.xpu.device_count()
            print(f"   XPU device count: {device_count}")
            print()
            
            # Get device information
            for i in range(device_count):
                device_name = torch.xpu.get_device_name(i)
                device_properties = torch.xpu.get_device_properties(i)
                
                print(f"   Device {i}: {device_name}")
                print(f"      Total memory: {device_properties.total_memory / (1024**3):.2f} GB")
                print(f"      Max compute units: {device_properties.max_compute_units}")
                print()
            
            # Test basic operations
            print("   Testing basic XPU operations...")
            try:
                # Create a tensor on XPU
                x = torch.randn(10, 10, device='xpu:0')
                y = torch.randn(10, 10, device='xpu:0')
                z = torch.matmul(x, y)
                
                print("   ✅ Tensor creation: SUCCESS")
                print("   ✅ Matrix multiplication: SUCCESS")
                print()
                
                # Get memory info
                memory_allocated = torch.xpu.memory_allocated(0) / (1024**2)
                memory_reserved = torch.xpu.memory_reserved(0) / (1024**2)
                print(f"   Memory allocated: {memory_allocated:.2f} MB")
                print(f"   Memory reserved: {memory_reserved:.2f} MB")
                print()
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"   ⚠️  Basic operations test failed: {e}")
                print()
            
            return True
        else:
            print("❌ XPU backend is NOT available")
            print()
            print("Possible issues:")
            print("   1. Level Zero runtime not installed")
            print("      Check: ls -la /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libze_loader.so")
            print("      Install: sudo apt-get install intel-level-zero-gpu")
            print()
            print("   2. GPU driver not loaded")
            print("      Check: lsmod | grep i915")
            print("      Load: sudo modprobe i915")
            print()
            print("   3. User not in 'render' group")
            print("      Check: groups | grep render")
            print("      Add: sudo usermod -aG render $USER")
            print("      Then: log out and back in")
            print()
            print("   4. DRI device not accessible")
            print("      Check: ls -la /dev/dri/renderD128")
            print("      Permissions should be: crw-rw---- render render")
            print()
            print("   5. No Intel GPU present")
            print("      Check: lspci | grep -i intel | grep -i vga")
            print()
            
            return False
            
    except AttributeError:
        print("❌ torch.xpu module not available")
        print("   This PyTorch build may not support XPU")
        print("   Ensure IPEX is properly installed")
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Error checking XPU: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        return False


def check_system_requirements():
    """Check system-level requirements."""
    print("Checking system requirements...")
    print("-" * 70)
    print()
    
    # Check for Intel GPU
    import subprocess
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(['lspci'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        if 'Intel' in result.stdout and ('VGA' in result.stdout or 'Display' in result.stdout):
            print("✅ Intel GPU detected via lspci")
        else:
            print("⚠️  Intel GPU not detected via lspci")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"⚠️  Could not check lspci: {e}")
    
    # Check for DRI device
    if os.path.exists('/dev/dri/renderD128'):
        print("✅ DRI render device found: /dev/dri/renderD128")
        stat = os.stat('/dev/dri/renderD128')
        print(f"   Permissions: {oct(stat.st_mode)[-3:]}")
    else:
        print("❌ DRI render device not found: /dev/dri/renderD128")
    
    # Check for Level Zero library
    level_zero_paths = [
        '/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libze_loader.so',
        '/usr/lib/libze_loader.so',
        '/usr/local/lib/libze_loader.so',
    ]
    
    found_lib = False
    for path in level_zero_paths:
        if os.path.exists(path):
            print(f"✅ Level Zero library found: {path}")
            found_lib = True
            break
    
    if not found_lib:
        print("❌ Level Zero library not found")
        print("   Install: sudo apt-get install intel-level-zero-gpu")
    
    # Check user groups
    try:
        import grp
        user_groups = [g.gr_name for g in grp.getgrall() if os.getlogin() in g.gr_mem]
        user_groups.append(grp.getgrgid(os.getgid()).gr_name)
        
        if 'render' in user_groups:
            print("✅ User is in 'render' group")
        else:
            print("❌ User is NOT in 'render' group")
            print("   Add: sudo usermod -aG render $USER")
            print("   Then: log out and back in")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"⚠️  Could not check user groups: {e}")
    
    # Check kernel driver
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(['lsmod'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        if 'i915' in result.stdout:
            print("✅ i915 kernel driver loaded")
        else:
            print("⚠️  i915 kernel driver not loaded")
            print("   Load: sudo modprobe i915")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"⚠️  Could not check kernel modules: {e}")
    
    print()


def main():
    """Main verification function."""
    # Check system requirements first
    check_system_requirements()
    
    print()
    print("=" * 70)
    print()
    
    # Check XPU availability
    success = check_xpu_availability()
    
    print("=" * 70)
    
    if success:
        print()
        print("✅ XPU verification PASSED")
        print()
        print("Your Intel GPU is ready for use with PyTorch!")
        print()
        print("Example usage:")
        print("  import torch")
        print("  import intel_extension_for_pytorch as ipex")
        print()
        print("  # Create tensor on XPU")
        print("  x = torch.randn(10, 10, device='xpu:0')")
        print()
        print("  # Run model on XPU")
        print("  model = model.to('xpu:0')")
        print("  output = model(input.to('xpu:0'))")
        print()
        return 0
    else:
        print()
        print("❌ XPU verification FAILED")
        print()
        print("See above for troubleshooting steps.")
        print()
        return 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/analysis/recovery/unlock/unlock/old_scripts/README.md

# Hardware Unlock Scripts

This directory contains scripts for hardware unlock procedures on the Dell Latitude 5450 system.

## Directory Structure

```
unlock/
├── common/          # Common utilities (XCR0 monitoring, direct execution tests)
├── ethernet/        # Ethernet controller unlock procedures
├── gna/            # GNA (Gaussian Neural Accelerator) unlock procedures
├── heci/            # HECI (Management Engine) unlock procedures
├── npu/             # NPU (Neural Processing Unit) unlock procedures
└── vsec/            # VSEC/PMT unlock procedures
```

## Common Utilities

- `monitor_xcr0.py` - Monitor XCR0 MSR for changes during unlock attempts
- `test_avx512_execution.c` - Direct AVX512 execution test (more reliable than CPUID)
- `test_amx_execution.c` - Direct AMX execution test (more reliable than CPUID)

## Ethernet Controller Unlock

The Ethernet controller (00:1f.6, Intel 8086:550a) has been identified as a potential hidden unlock pathway with 13 writable registers.

### Key Scripts

- `test_ethernet_baseline.py` - Capture baseline system state
- `backup_eth_registers.py` - Backup all writable registers
- `restore_eth_registers.py` - Restore registers from backup
- `test_eth_0x0200_unlock.py` - Test Engineering Mode register (highest priority)
- `test_eth_0x0024_unlock.py` - Test suspicious register (0xA0000007 pattern)
- `test_eth_all_writable.py` - Test all 13 writable registers
- `test_eth_combined_*.py` - Combined unlock sequence tests
- `test_eth_vsec_coord.py` - Coordinate with VSEC/PMT unlock
- `test_eth_gna_coord.py` - Coordinate with GNA unlock
- `test_eth_multi_device_unlock.py` - Multi-device unlock sequence

### Documentation

See `FLAGS/working/kernel_6.19_clean_install/unlock/` for:
- `ETHERNET_UNLOCK_RESULTS.md` - Test results tracking
- `ETHERNET_UNLOCK_PROCEDURE.md` - Final unlock procedure
- `ETHERNET_IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md` - Implementation summary

## VSEC/PMT Unlock

The VSEC/PMT device (00:0a.0, Intel 8086:7d0d) already shows `0xDEADBEEF` (bypass active) at registers 0x0000 and 0x000C.

### Key Scripts

- `test_vsec_baseline.py` - Capture baseline system state
- `backup_vsec_registers.py` - Backup VSEC registers
- `restore_vsec_registers.py` - Restore registers from backup
- `test_vsec_0x0000_unlock.py` - Test Control/Status 0 register
- `test_vsec_0x000C_unlock.py` - Test Bypass register
- `test_vsec_combined_unlock.py` - Combined unlock sequence
- `test_vsec_ethernet_coord.py` - VSEC + Ethernet coordination
- `scan_vsec_regions.py` - Scan for writable registers

## Usage

All scripts require root privileges:

```bash
# Ethernet unlock
sudo ./ethernet/test_ethernet_baseline.py
sudo ./ethernet/backup_eth_registers.py
sudo ./ethernet/test_eth_0x0200_unlock.py

# VSEC unlock
sudo ./vsec/test_vsec_baseline.py
sudo ./vsec/backup_vsec_registers.py
sudo ./vsec/test_vsec_0x000C_unlock.py
```

## Safety

- Always backup registers before testing
- Scripts automatically restore original values
- Network connectivity is monitored
- Direct execution tests verify CPU feature changes

## Success Criteria

- XCR0 MSR shows AVX512/AMX bits enabled
- Direct execution tests pass (no "Illegal instruction")
- CPU features actually work (not just CPUID flags)
- Network connectivity maintained
- System stability preserved

## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/analysis/recovery/unlock/unlock/old_scripts/tpm/README.md

# TPM Memory Scanner - ME-TPM Coordination Bypass

Rust-based memory scanner for TPM (Trusted Platform Module) memory structures, focusing on ME-TPM coordination for unlock/bypass pathways.

## Overview

This scanner probes TPM memory regions to identify:
- Interesting registers (non-zero, non-0xFFFFFFFF values)
- Writable registers (accepts unlock patterns)
- Existing unlock patterns (Engineering Mode, Bypass, etc.)
- ME-TPM shared memory coordination areas

## TPM Device Information

- **Device**: STM0176:00 (STM TPM 2.0)
- **Driver**: `tpm_tis`
- **MMIO Base**: `0xFED40000` (from `/proc/iomem`)
- **MMIO Size**: `0x5000` (20KB)
- **Device Files**: `/dev/tpm0`, `/dev/tpmrm0`

## Usage

```bash
# Build
cd scripts/unlock/tpm
cargo build --release

# Scan TPM TIS interface
sudo ./target/release/tpm_scanner --tis --test-writes --test-unlock

# Scan ME-TPM shared memory region
sudo ./target/release/tpm_scanner --me-shared --test-writes --test-unlock

# Scan all regions
sudo ./target/release/tpm_scanner --tis --me-shared --test-writes --test-unlock

# Custom region
sudo ./target/release/tpm_scanner --custom-base 0x5019000000 --custom-size 0x100000

# Verbose output
sudo ./target/release/tpm_scanner --tis --verbose

# JSON output
sudo ./target/release/tpm_scanner --tis --json
```

## Options

- `--tis`: Scan TPM TIS (Trusted Interface Standard) interface
- `--crb`: Scan TPM CRB (Command Response Buffer) interface
- `--me-shared`: Scan ME-TPM shared memory region
- `--custom-base <hex>`: Scan custom base address
- `--custom-size <bytes>`: Custom size (default: 8192)
- `--chunk-size <bytes>`: Chunk size for scanning (default: 4096)
- `--test-writes`: Test writability of registers
- `--test-unlock`: Check for existing unlock patterns
- `--json`: Output results as JSON
- `--verbose`: Verbose output

## Unlock Patterns Detected

- `0xA00A00A0`: Engineering Mode
- `0xDEADBEEF`: Bypass
- `0xDEADC0DE`: Bypass Alternative
- `0x55555555`: Unlock
- `0xFFFFFFFF`: Enable

## ME-TPM Coordination

The scanner focuses on ME-TPM coordination areas where:
- Intel ME (Management Engine) communicates with TPM
- Security policies are enforced
- Unlock/bypass mechanisms may exist
- Shared memory regions coordinate security state

## Safety

- Uses memory-safe Rust implementation
- Tests writability before modifying registers
- Restores original values after testing
- Requires root access for `/dev/mem`

## Integration

This scanner complements:
- HECI unlock tools (ME communication)
- VSEC/PMT unlock (hardware bypass)
- GNA unlock (auxiliary pathway)
- Ethernet unlock (hidden pathway)

## Notes

- TPM is a security-critical component - use with caution
- ME-TPM coordination is Intel-specific
- Some regions may require driver unbinding
- Results may vary based on TPM firmware version

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Analyze Ethernet Controller Register Clusters
Analyzes 71 register clusters found
Looks for structured data patterns
May reveal unlock sequence requirements
"""

import os
import sys
import mmap
import struct

ETH_BASE = 0x7c100000
ETH_SIZE = 0x20000  # 128K

def main():
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Ethernet Controller Register Cluster Analysis")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print("\n✗ Must run as root")
        return 1
    
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, ETH_SIZE, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                        mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=ETH_BASE)
        os.close(mem_fd)
        
        print(f"\nScanning for register clusters...")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        clusters = []
        cluster_start = None
        cluster_values = []
        
        for offset in range(0, min(ETH_SIZE, 0x10000), 4):  # Scan first 64KB
            mmio.seek(offset)
            value = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
            
            if value != 0 and value != 0xFFFFFFFF:
                if cluster_start is None:
                    cluster_start = offset
                    cluster_values = [value]
                else:
                    if offset == cluster_start + len(cluster_values) * 4:
                        cluster_values.append(value)
                    else:
                        if len(cluster_values) > 4:
                            clusters.append((cluster_start, cluster_values))
                        cluster_start = offset
                        cluster_values = [value]
            else:
                if cluster_start is not None and len(cluster_values) > 4:
                    clusters.append((cluster_start, cluster_values))
                cluster_start = None
                cluster_values = []
        
        if cluster_start is not None and len(cluster_values) > 4:
            clusters.append((cluster_start, cluster_values))
        
        print(f"\nFound {len(clusters)} register clusters (5+ consecutive non-zero registers)")
        
        if clusters:
            print("\nLargest clusters:")
            clusters_sorted = sorted(clusters, key=lambda x: len(x[1]), reverse=True)
            for start, values in clusters_sorted[:10]:
                print(f"\n  Cluster at 0x{start:04X}: {len(values)} consecutive registers")
                print(f"    First 8 values:")
                for i, val in enumerate(values[:8]):
                    print(f"      0x{start+i*4:04X}: 0x{val:08X}")
            
            print("\n⚠ These clusters may indicate structured data or unlock sequences")
        else:
            print("\nNo significant clusters found")
        
        mmio.close()
        return 0
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n✗ Error: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        return 1

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())



## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/analysis/recovery/unlock/unlock/old_scripts/ethernet/test_eth_multi_device_unlock.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Test Multi-Device Unlock Sequence
Coordinates VSEC/PMT, GNA, and Ethernet controller unlocks
Sequence:
1. Verify VSEC/PMT: 0xDEADBEEF
2. Verify GNA: 0xFFFFFFFF
3. Write Ethernet 0x0200: 0xA00A00A0
4. Write Ethernet 0x0024: 0xA00A00A0
5. Check CPU features via direct execution
"""

import os
import sys
import mmap
import struct
import subprocess
import time
import json

ETH_BASE = 0x7c100000
ETH_SIZE = 0x20000
ETH_ENG_MODE = 0x0200
ETH_SUSPICIOUS = 0x0024

VSEC_BASE = 0x5019240000
VSEC_SIZE = 0x1000

GNA_BASE = 0x50192e3000
GNA_SIZE = 0x1000
GNA_REG = 0x00B0

def check_msr_xcr0():
    """Check XCR0 MSR"""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(['rdmsr', '0x1D'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        if result.returncode == 0:
            return int(result.stdout.strip(), 16)
    except:
        pass
    return None

def run_direct_execution_test(test_binary):
    """Run direct execution test and return results"""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run([test_binary], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
        return {
            'returncode': result.returncode,
            'success': result.returncode == 0 and 'Illegal instruction' not in result.stderr
        }
    except:
        return {'success': False}

def compile_test_binaries():
    """Compile AVX512 and AMX test binaries if needed"""
    avx512_bin = '/tmp/test_avx512_execution'
    amx_bin = '/tmp/test_amx_execution'
    
    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    
    if not os.path.exists(avx512_bin):
        source = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(script_dir), 'common', 'test_avx512_execution.c')
        if os.path.exists(source):
            subprocess.run(['gcc', '-mavx512f', '-mavx512bw', '-mavx512vl', 
                          '-o', avx512_bin, source], 
                         capture_output=True)
    
    if not os.path.exists(amx_bin):
        source = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(script_dir), 'common', 'test_amx_execution.c')
        if os.path.exists(source):
            subprocess.run(['gcc', '-mamx-tile', '-mamx-int8', 
                          '-o', amx_bin, source], 
                         capture_output=True)
    
    return avx512_bin, amx_bin

def read_device_register(base, size, offset):
    """Read register from device"""
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, size, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                        mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=base)
        os.close(mem_fd)
        
        mmio.seek(offset)
        value = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
        mmio.close()
        return f'0x{value:08X}'
    except:
        return None

def main():
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Multi-Device Unlock Sequence Test")
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Coordinates VSEC/PMT, GNA, and Ethernet controller")
    
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print("\n✗ Must run as root")
        return 1
    
    # Compile test binaries
    print("\n[1] Compiling direct execution tests...")
    avx512_bin, amx_bin = compile_test_binaries()
    
    # Baseline
    print("\n[2] Capturing baseline state...")
    xcr0_before = check_msr_xcr0()
    avx512_before = run_direct_execution_test(avx512_bin)
    amx_before = run_direct_execution_test(amx_bin)
    print(f"  XCR0: {f'0x{xcr0_before:016X}' if xcr0_before else 'N/A'}")
    print(f"  AVX512: {'✓' if avx512_before['success'] else '✗'}")
    print(f"  AMX: {'✓' if amx_before['success'] else '✗'}")
    
    # Step 1: Verify VSEC/PMT
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("[3] Step 1: Verifying VSEC/PMT status")
    print('='*70)
    vsec_status = read_device_register(VSEC_BASE, VSEC_SIZE, 0)
    print(f"  VSEC/PMT: {vsec_status or 'N/A'}")
    if vsec_status == '0xDEADBEEF':
        print("  ✓ VSEC/PMT shows bypass active")
    else:
        print("  ⚠ VSEC/PMT does not show expected bypass pattern")
    
    # Step 2: Verify GNA
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("[4] Step 2: Verifying GNA status")
    print('='*70)
    gna_status = read_device_register(GNA_BASE, GNA_SIZE, GNA_REG)
    print(f"  GNA 0x00B0: {gna_status or 'N/A'}")
    if gna_status == '0xFFFFFFFF':
        print("  ✓ GNA shows unlock state")
    else:
        print("  ⚠ GNA does not show expected unlock state")
    
    # Step 3-4: Write Ethernet registers
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("[5] Step 3-4: Writing Ethernet unlock registers")
    print('='*70)
    
    # Map Ethernet MMIO
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        eth_mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, ETH_SIZE, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                            mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=ETH_BASE)
        os.close(mem_fd)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  ✗ Failed to map MMIO: {e}")
        return 1
    
    # Read original values
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_ENG_MODE)
    original_0x0200 = struct.unpack('<I', eth_mmio.read(4))[0]
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_SUSPICIOUS)
    original_0x0024 = struct.unpack('<I', eth_mmio.read(4))[0]
    
    print(f"  Original values:")
    print(f"    0x{ETH_ENG_MODE:04X}: 0x{original_0x0200:08X}")
    print(f"    0x{ETH_SUSPICIOUS:04X}: 0x{original_0x0024:08X}")
    
    # Write unlock pattern
    test_pattern = 0xA00A00A0
    print(f"\n  Writing 0x{test_pattern:08X} to both registers...")
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_ENG_MODE)
    eth_mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', test_pattern))
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_SUSPICIOUS)
    eth_mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', test_pattern))
    time.sleep(0.5)  # Wait for coordinated unlock
    
    # Verify writes
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_ENG_MODE)
    readback_0x0200 = struct.unpack('<I', eth_mmio.read(4))[0]
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_SUSPICIOUS)
    readback_0x0024 = struct.unpack('<I', eth_mmio.read(4))[0]
    
    write_success = (readback_0x0200 == test_pattern and readback_0x0024 == test_pattern)
    print(f"  Write success: {'✓' if write_success else '✗'}")
    
    if not write_success:
        print(f"    Readback: 0x{ETH_ENG_MODE:04X}=0x{readback_0x0200:08X}, 0x{ETH_SUSPICIOUS:04X}=0x{readback_0x0024:08X}")
        eth_mmio.close()
        return 1
    
    # Step 5: Check CPU features
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("[6] Step 5: Checking CPU features")
    print('='*70)
    
    # Check XCR0
    xcr0_after = check_msr_xcr0()
    xcr0_changed = (xcr0_after and xcr0_after != xcr0_before)
    if xcr0_changed:
        print(f"  ⚠ XCR0 CHANGED!")
        print(f"    Before: 0x{xcr0_before:016X}")
        print(f"    After:  0x{xcr0_after:016X}")
    else:
        print(f"  → XCR0 unchanged")
    
    # Run direct execution tests
    print("\n  Running direct execution tests...")
    avx512_after = run_direct_execution_test(avx512_bin)
    amx_after = run_direct_execution_test(amx_bin)
    
    avx512_changed = (avx512_before['success'] != avx512_after['success'])
    amx_changed = (amx_before['success'] != amx_after['success'])
    
    print(f"    AVX512: {'✓' if avx512_after['success'] else '✗'} ({'CHANGED' if avx512_changed else 'unchanged'})")
    print(f"    AMX: {'✓' if amx_after['success'] else '✗'} ({'CHANGED' if amx_changed else 'unchanged'})")
    
    if xcr0_changed or avx512_changed or amx_changed:
        print(f"\n    ⚠⚠⚠ MULTI-DEVICE UNLOCK EFFECTS DETECTED ⚠⚠⚠")
    
    # Restore original values
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("[7] Restoring original Ethernet register values")
    print('='*70)
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_ENG_MODE)
    eth_mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original_0x0200))
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_SUSPICIOUS)
    eth_mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original_0x0024))
    
    eth_mmio.close()
    
    # Save results
    output_file = '/tmp/eth_multi_device_unlock_results.json'
    with open(output_file, 'w') as f:
        json.dump({
            'device_status': {
                'vsec_pmt': vsec_status,
                'gna': gna_status
            },
            'ethernet_registers': {
                '0x0200': f'0x{original_0x0200:08X}',
                '0x0024': f'0x{original_0x0024:08X}'
            },
            'baseline': {
                'xcr0': f'0x{xcr0_before:016X}' if xcr0_before else None,
                'avx512_success': avx512_before['success'],
                'amx_success': amx_before['success']
            },
            'results': {
                'write_success': write_success,
                'xcr0_changed': xcr0_changed,
                'xcr0_after': f'0x{xcr0_after:016X}' if xcr0_after else None,
                'avx512_changed': avx512_changed,
                'avx512_success': avx512_after['success'],
                'amx_changed': amx_changed,
                'amx_success': amx_after['success']
            }
        }, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("Test Complete")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Results saved to: {output_file}")
    
    return 0

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())



## SOURCE: intel-bug-bounty-report/analysis/recovery/unlock/unlock/old_scripts/ethernet/test_eth_full_unlock.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Test Ethernet Controller Full Unlock Sequence
Writes unlock patterns to all 13 writable registers simultaneously
Tests if multiple registers must be set for unlock
Includes direct execution testing for CPU feature verification
"""

import os
import sys
import mmap
import struct
import subprocess
import time
import json

ETH_BASE = 0x7c100000
ETH_SIZE = 0x20000

WRITABLE_REGS = [
    (0x0010, 'Control/Status'),
    (0x0014, 'Control 5'),
    (0x0024, 'Control 9 (Suspicious)'),
    (0x0028, 'Control 10'),
    (0x0030, 'Control 12'),
    (0x003C, 'Control 15'),
    (0x0040, 'Control 16'),
    (0x00E4, 'Control 57'),
    (0x00E8, 'Control 58'),
    (0x00FC, 'Control 63'),
    (0x0110, 'Control 68'),
    (0x0200, 'Engineering Mode'),
    (0x0420, 'Control 264'),
]

def check_msr_xcr0():
    """Check XCR0 MSR"""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(['rdmsr', '0x1D'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        if result.returncode == 0:
            return int(result.stdout.strip(), 16)
    except:
        pass
    return None

def run_direct_execution_test(test_binary):
    """Run direct execution test and return results"""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run([test_binary], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
        return {
            'returncode': result.returncode,
            'success': result.returncode == 0 and 'Illegal instruction' not in result.stderr
        }
    except:
        return {'success': False}

def compile_test_binaries():
    """Compile AVX512 and AMX test binaries if needed"""
    avx512_bin = '/tmp/test_avx512_execution'
    amx_bin = '/tmp/test_amx_execution'
    
    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    
    if not os.path.exists(avx512_bin):
        source = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(script_dir), 'common', 'test_avx512_execution.c')
        if os.path.exists(source):
            subprocess.run(['gcc', '-mavx512f', '-mavx512bw', '-mavx512vl', 
                          '-o', avx512_bin, source], 
                         capture_output=True)
    
    if not os.path.exists(amx_bin):
        source = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(script_dir), 'common', 'test_amx_execution.c')
        if os.path.exists(source):
            subprocess.run(['gcc', '-mamx-tile', '-mamx-int8', 
                          '-o', amx_bin, source], 
                         capture_output=True)
    
    return avx512_bin, amx_bin

def main():
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Ethernet Controller Full Unlock Sequence Test")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Testing all {len(WRITABLE_REGS)} writable registers simultaneously")
    
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print("\n✗ Must run as root")
        return 1
    
    # Compile test binaries
    print("\n[1] Compiling direct execution tests...")
    avx512_bin, amx_bin = compile_test_binaries()
    
    # Baseline
    print("\n[2] Capturing baseline state...")
    xcr0_before = check_msr_xcr0()
    avx512_before = run_direct_execution_test(avx512_bin)
    amx_before = run_direct_execution_test(amx_bin)
    print(f"  XCR0: {f'0x{xcr0_before:016X}' if xcr0_before else 'N/A'}")
    print(f"  AVX512: {'✓' if avx512_before['success'] else '✗'}")
    print(f"  AMX: {'✓' if amx_before['success'] else '✗'}")
    
    # Map MMIO
    print("\n[3] Mapping Ethernet controller MMIO...")
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, ETH_SIZE, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                        mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=ETH_BASE)
        os.close(mem_fd)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  ✗ Failed to map MMIO: {e}")
        return 1
    
    # Read and save original values
    original_values = {}
    print("\n[4] Reading original register values...")
    for offset, name in WRITABLE_REGS:
        mmio.seek(offset)
        original_values[offset] = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
        print(f"  0x{offset:04X} ({name}): 0x{original_values[offset]:08X}")
    
    # Test unlock patterns
    test_patterns = [
        (0xA00A00A0, "Engineering mode magic (all registers)"),
        (0xDEADBEEF, "Security bypass magic (all registers)"),
    ]
    
    results = []
    
    for pattern, description in test_patterns:
        print(f"\n{'='*70}")
        print(f"[5] Testing: {description} (0x{pattern:08X})")
        print('='*70)
        
        # Write all registers
        print("  Writing to all registers...")
        write_success = True
        for offset, name in WRITABLE_REGS:
            mmio.seek(offset)
            mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', pattern))
        
        time.sleep(0.5)  # Longer wait for full unlock sequence
        
        # Verify all writes
        print("  Verifying writes...")
        failed_writes = []
        for offset, name in WRITABLE_REGS:
            mmio.seek(offset)
            readback = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
            if readback != pattern:
                failed_writes.append((offset, name, readback))
                write_success = False
        
        if failed_writes:
            print(f"  ✗ {len(failed_writes)} registers failed to write:")
            for offset, name, readback in failed_writes:
                print(f"    0x{offset:04X} ({name}): 0x{readback:08X}")
        else:
            print(f"  ✓ All {len(WRITABLE_REGS)} registers written successfully")
        
        results.append({
            'pattern': f'0x{pattern:08X}',
            'description': description,
            'write_success': write_success,
            'failed_writes': [{'offset': f'0x{o:04X}', 'name': n, 'readback': f'0x{r:08X}'} 
                            for o, n, r in failed_writes] if failed_writes else []
        })
        
        if not write_success:
            # Restore all
            for offset, _ in WRITABLE_REGS:
                mmio.seek(offset)
                mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original_values[offset]))
            continue
        
        # Check XCR0
        xcr0_after = check_msr_xcr0()
        xcr0_changed = (xcr0_after and xcr0_after != xcr0_before)
        if xcr0_changed:
            print(f"\n  ⚠ XCR0 CHANGED!")
            print(f"    Before: 0x{xcr0_before:016X}")
            print(f"    After:  0x{xcr0_after:016X}")
            results[-1]['xcr0_changed'] = True
            results[-1]['xcr0_after'] = f'0x{xcr0_after:016X}'
        else:
            print(f"\n  → XCR0 unchanged")
            results[-1]['xcr0_changed'] = False
        
        # Run direct execution tests
        print("\n  [6] Running direct execution tests...")
        avx512_after = run_direct_execution_test(avx512_bin)
        amx_after = run_direct_execution_test(amx_bin)
        
        avx512_changed = (avx512_before['success'] != avx512_after['success'])
        amx_changed = (amx_before['success'] != amx_after['success'])
        
        print(f"    AVX512: {'✓' if avx512_after['success'] else '✗'} ({'CHANGED' if avx512_changed else 'unchanged'})")
        print(f"    AMX: {'✓' if amx_after['success'] else '✗'} ({'CHANGED' if amx_changed else 'unchanged'})")
        
        results[-1]['avx512_success'] = avx512_after['success']
        results[-1]['amx_success'] = amx_after['success']
        results[-1]['avx512_changed'] = avx512_changed
        results[-1]['amx_changed'] = amx_changed
        
        if xcr0_changed or avx512_changed or amx_changed:
            print(f"\n    ⚠⚠⚠ FULL UNLOCK EFFECTS DETECTED ⚠⚠⚠")
        
        # Restore all original values
        print("\n  [7] Restoring original values...")
        for offset, _ in WRITABLE_REGS:
            mmio.seek(offset)
            mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original_values[offset]))
        
        time.sleep(0.3)
    
    mmio.close()
    
    # Save results
    output_file = '/tmp/eth_full_unlock_results.json'
    with open(output_file, 'w') as f:
        json.dump({
            'num_registers': len(WRITABLE_REGS),
            'baseline': {
                'xcr0': f'0x{xcr0_before:016X}' if xcr0_before else None,
                'avx512_success': avx512_before['success'],
                'amx_success': amx_before['success']
            },
            'results': results
        }, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("Test Complete")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Results saved to: {output_file}")
    
    # Summary
    print("\nSummary:")
    for result in results:
        print(f"  {result['description']}:")
        print(f"    Write success: {result.get('write_success', False)}")
        if result.get('failed_writes'):
            print(f"    Failed writes: {len(result['failed_writes'])}")
        print(f"    XCR0 changed: {result.get('xcr0_changed', False)}")
        print(f"    AVX512 changed: {result.get('avx512_changed', False)}")
        print(f"    AMX changed: {result.get('amx_changed', False)}")
    
    return 0

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Backup Ethernet Controller Writable Registers
Saves all 13 writable registers to JSON for restoration
"""

import os
import sys
import mmap
import struct
import json
from datetime import datetime

ETH_BASE = 0x7c100000
ETH_SIZE = 0x20000  # 128K

WRITABLE_REGS = [
    (0x0010, 'Control/Status'),
    (0x0014, 'Control 5'),
    (0x0024, 'Control 9 (Suspicious)'),
    (0x0028, 'Control 10'),
    (0x0030, 'Control 12'),
    (0x003C, 'Control 15'),
    (0x0040, 'Control 16'),
    (0x00E4, 'Control 57'),
    (0x00E8, 'Control 58'),
    (0x00FC, 'Control 63'),
    (0x0110, 'Control 68'),
    (0x0200, 'Engineering Mode'),
    (0x0420, 'Control 264'),
]

def backup_registers():
    """Backup all writable registers"""
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, ETH_SIZE, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                        mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=ETH_BASE)
        os.close(mem_fd)
        
        backup = {
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'device': '00:1f.6 (Intel 8086:550a)',
            'base': f'0x{ETH_BASE:016X}',
            'registers': {}
        }
        
        for offset, name in WRITABLE_REGS:
            mmio.seek(offset)
            value = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
            backup['registers'][f'0x{offset:04X}'] = {
                'name': name,
                'value': f'0x{value:08X}',
                'value_int': value
            }
        
        mmio.close()
        return backup
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error backing up registers: {e}")
        return None

def main():
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Ethernet Controller Register Backup")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print("\n✗ Must run as root")
        return 1
    
    backup = backup_registers()
    if not backup:
        return 1
    
    print("\nBacked up registers:")
    for offset, reg_data in backup['registers'].items():
        print(f"  {offset} ({reg_data['name']}): {reg_data['value']}")
    
    # Save to JSON
    output_file = '/tmp/ethernet_registers_backup.json'
    with open(output_file, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(backup, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print(f"Backup saved to: {output_file}")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    return 0

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

"""

"""

import os

import struct
import subprocess
import time
import json

ETH_BASE = 0x7c100000
ETH_SIZE = 0x20000
ETH_ENG_MODE = 0x0200
ETH_SUSPICIOUS = 0x0024

GNA_BASE = 0x50192e3000
GNA_SIZE = 0x1000
GNA_REG = 0x00B0

def check_msr_xcr0():
    """Check XCR0 MSR"""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(['rdmsr', '0x1D'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        if result.returncode == 0:
            return int(result.stdout.strip(), 16)
    except:
        pass
    return None

def run_direct_execution_test(test_binary):
    """Run direct execution test and return results"""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run([test_binary], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
        return {
            'returncode': result.returncode,
            'success': result.returncode == 0 and 'Illegal instruction' not in result.stderr
        }
    except:
        return {'success': False}

def compile_test_binaries():
    """Compile AVX512 and AMX test binaries if needed"""
    avx512_bin = '/tmp/test_avx512_execution'
    amx_bin = '/tmp/test_amx_execution'
    
    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    
    if not os.path.exists(avx512_bin):
        source = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(script_dir), 'common', 'test_avx512_execution.c')
        if os.path.exists(source):
            subprocess.run(['gcc', '-mavx512f', '-mavx512bw', '-mavx512vl', 
                          '-o', avx512_bin, source], 
                         capture_output=True)
    
    if not os.path.exists(amx_bin):
        source = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(script_dir), 'common', 'test_amx_execution.c')
        if os.path.exists(source):
            subprocess.run(['gcc', '-mamx-tile', '-mamx-int8', 
                          '-o', amx_bin, source], 
                         capture_output=True)
    
    return avx512_bin, amx_bin

def check_gna_status():
    """Check GNA status"""
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, GNA_SIZE, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                        mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=GNA_BASE)
        os.close(mem_fd)
        
        mmio.seek(GNA_REG)
        value = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
        mmio.close()
        return f'0x{value:08X}'
    except:
        return None

def main():
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Ethernet Controller + GNA Coordination Test")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print("\n✗ Must run as root")
        return 1
    
    # Check GNA status
    print("\n[1] Checking GNA status...")
    gna_status = check_gna_status()
    print(f"  GNA 0x00B0: {gna_status or 'N/A'}")
    
    if gna_status != '0xFFFFFFFF':
        print("  ⚠ GNA does not show expected unlock state (0xFFFFFFFF)")
    
    # Compile test binaries
    print("\n[2] Compiling direct execution tests...")
    avx512_bin, amx_bin = compile_test_binaries()
    
    # Baseline
    print("\n[3] Capturing baseline state...")
    xcr0_before = check_msr_xcr0()
    avx512_before = run_direct_execution_test(avx512_bin)
    amx_before = run_direct_execution_test(amx_bin)
    print(f"  XCR0: {f'0x{xcr0_before:016X}' if xcr0_before else 'N/A'}")
    print(f"  AVX512: {'✓' if avx512_before['success'] else '✗'}")
    print(f"  AMX: {'✓' if amx_before['success'] else '✗'}")
    
    # Map Ethernet MMIO
    print("\n[4] Mapping Ethernet controller MMIO...")
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        eth_mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, ETH_SIZE, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                            mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=ETH_BASE)
        os.close(mem_fd)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  ✗ Failed to map MMIO: {e}")
        return 1
    
    # Read original Ethernet register values
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_ENG_MODE)
    original_0x0200 = struct.unpack('<I', eth_mmio.read(4))[0]
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_SUSPICIOUS)
    original_0x0024 = struct.unpack('<I', eth_mmio.read(4))[0]
    
    print(f"\n[5] Original Ethernet register values:")
    print(f"  0x{ETH_ENG_MODE:04X}: 0x{original_0x0200:08X}")
    print(f"  0x{ETH_SUSPICIOUS:04X}: 0x{original_0x0024:08X}")
    
    # Test Ethernet unlock with GNA active
    test_pattern = 0xA00A00A0  # Engineering mode magic
    
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print(f"[6] Testing Ethernet unlock (0x{test_pattern:08X}) with GNA active")
    print('='*70)
    
    # Write to both Ethernet registers
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_ENG_MODE)
    eth_mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', test_pattern))
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_SUSPICIOUS)
    eth_mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', test_pattern))
    time.sleep(0.3)
    
    # Verify writes
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_ENG_MODE)
    readback_0x0200 = struct.unpack('<I', eth_mmio.read(4))[0]
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_SUSPICIOUS)
    readback_0x0024 = struct.unpack('<I', eth_mmio.read(4))[0]
    
    write_success = (readback_0x0200 == test_pattern and readback_0x0024 == test_pattern)
    print(f"  Write success: {'✓' if write_success else '✗'}")
    
    if not write_success:
        print(f"    Readback: 0x{ETH_ENG_MODE:04X}=0x{readback_0x0200:08X}, 0x{ETH_SUSPICIOUS:04X}=0x{readback_0x0024:08X}")
        eth_mmio.close()
        return 1
    
    # Check XCR0
    xcr0_after = check_msr_xcr0()
    xcr0_changed = (xcr0_after and xcr0_after != xcr0_before)
    if xcr0_changed:
        print(f"\n  ⚠ XCR0 CHANGED!")
        print(f"    Before: 0x{xcr0_before:016X}")
        print(f"    After:  0x{xcr0_after:016X}")
    else:
        print(f"\n  → XCR0 unchanged")
    
    # Run direct execution tests
    print("\n  [7] Running direct execution tests...")
    avx512_after = run_direct_execution_test(avx512_bin)
    amx_after = run_direct_execution_test(amx_bin)
    
    avx512_changed = (avx512_before['success'] != avx512_after['success'])
    amx_changed = (amx_before['success'] != amx_after['success'])
    
    print(f"    AVX512: {'✓' if avx512_after['success'] else '✗'} ({'CHANGED' if avx512_changed else 'unchanged'})")
    print(f"    AMX: {'✓' if amx_after['success'] else '✗'} ({'CHANGED' if amx_changed else 'unchanged'})")
    
    if xcr0_changed or avx512_changed or amx_changed:
        print(f"\n    ⚠⚠⚠ COORDINATED UNLOCK EFFECTS DETECTED ⚠⚠⚠")
    
    # Restore original values
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("[8] Restoring original Ethernet register values")
    print('='*70)
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_ENG_MODE)
    eth_mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original_0x0200))
    eth_mmio.seek(ETH_SUSPICIOUS)
    eth_mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original_0x0024))
    
    eth_mmio.close()
    
    # Save results
    output_file = '/tmp/eth_gna_coord_results.json'
    with open(output_file, 'w') as f:
        json.dump({
            'gna_status': gna_status,
            'ethernet_registers': {
                '0x0200': f'0x{original_0x0200:08X}',
                '0x0024': f'0x{original_0x0024:08X}'
            },
            'baseline': {
                'xcr0': f'0x{xcr0_before:016X}' if xcr0_before else None,
                'avx512_success': avx512_before['success'],
                'amx_success': amx_before['success']
            },
            'results': {
                'write_success': write_success,
                'xcr0_changed': xcr0_changed,
                'xcr0_after': f'0x{xcr0_after:016X}' if xcr0_after else None,
                'avx512_changed': avx512_changed,
                'avx512_success': avx512_after['success'],
                'amx_changed': amx_changed,
                'amx_success': amx_after['success']
            }
        }, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("Test Complete")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Results saved to: {output_file}")
    
    return 0

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Explore Ethernet Controller Pointer-Like Values
Follows pointer-like values (0x40000000-0x5FFFFFFF range)
May point to hidden computing engine memory
"""

import os
import sys
import mmap
import struct

ETH_BASE = 0x7c100000
ETH_SIZE = 0x20000  # 128K

def main():
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Ethernet Controller Pointer-Like Value Exploration")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print("\n✗ Must run as root")
        return 1
    
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, ETH_SIZE, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                        mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=ETH_BASE)
        os.close(mem_fd)
        
        print(f"\nScanning for pointer-like values (0x40000000-0x5FFFFFFF)...")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        pointers = []
        for offset in range(0, ETH_SIZE, 4):
            mmio.seek(offset)
            value = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
            
            if 0x40000000 <= value <= 0x5FFFFFFF:
                pointers.append((offset, value))
        
        print(f"\nFound {len(pointers)} pointer-like values")
        
        if pointers:
            print("\nFirst 20 pointer-like values:")
            for offset, value in pointers[:20]:
                print(f"  0x{offset:08X}: 0x{value:08X}")
            
            print("\n⚠ These may point to hidden computing engine memory regions")
            print("  Further investigation needed to follow these pointers")
        else:
            print("\nNo pointer-like values found")
        
        mmio.close()
        return 0
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n✗ Error: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        return 1

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

        }
    except:
        return {'success': False}

def compile_test_binaries():
    """Compile AVX512 and AMX test binaries if needed"""
    avx512_bin = '/tmp/test_avx512_execution'
    amx_bin = '/tmp/test_amx_execution'
    
    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    
    if not os.path.exists(avx512_bin):
        source = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(script_dir), 'common', 'test_avx512_execution.c')
        if os.path.exists(source):
            subprocess.run(['gcc', '-mavx512f', '-mavx512bw', '-mavx512vl', 
                          '-o', avx512_bin, source], 
                         capture_output=True)
    
    if not os.path.exists(amx_bin):
        source = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(script_dir), 'common', 'test_amx_execution.c')
        if os.path.exists(source):
            subprocess.run(['gcc', '-mamx-tile', '-mamx-int8', 
                          '-o', amx_bin, source], 
                         capture_output=True)
    
    return avx512_bin, amx_bin

def main():
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Ethernet Controller Three-Register Combined Unlock Test")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Testing: 0x{REG1[0]:04X} ({REG1[1]}) + 0x{REG2[0]:04X} ({REG2[1]}) + 0x{REG3[0]:04X} ({REG3[1]})")
    
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print("\n✗ Must run as root")
        return 1
    
    # Compile test binaries
    print("\n[1] Compiling direct execution tests...")
    avx512_bin, amx_bin = compile_test_binaries()
    
    # Baseline
    print("\n[2] Capturing baseline state...")
    xcr0_before = check_msr_xcr0()
    avx512_before = run_direct_execution_test(avx512_bin)
    amx_before = run_direct_execution_test(amx_bin)
    print(f"  XCR0: {f'0x{xcr0_before:016X}' if xcr0_before else 'N/A'}")
    print(f"  AVX512: {'✓' if avx512_before['success'] else '✗'}")
    print(f"  AMX: {'✓' if amx_before['success'] else '✗'}")
    
    # Map MMIO
    print("\n[3] Mapping Ethernet controller MMIO...")
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, ETH_SIZE, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                        mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=ETH_BASE)
        os.close(mem_fd)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  ✗ Failed to map MMIO: {e}")
        return 1
    
    # Read original values
    mmio.seek(REG1[0])
    original1 = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
    mmio.seek(REG2[0])
    original2 = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
    mmio.seek(REG3[0])
    original3 = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
    
    print(f"\n[4] Original values:")
    print(f"  0x{REG1[0]:04X}: 0x{original1:08X}")
    print(f"  0x{REG2[0]:04X}: 0x{original2:08X}")
    print(f"  0x{REG3[0]:04X}: 0x{original3:08X}")
    
    # Test different patterns
    test_patterns = [
        (0xA00A00A0, "Engineering mode magic (all three)"),
        (0xDEADBEEF, "Security bypass magic (all three)"),
    ]
    
    results = []
    
    for pattern, description in test_patterns:
        print(f"\n{'='*70}")
        print(f"[5] Testing: {description} (0x{pattern:08X})")
        print('='*70)
        
        # Write all three registers simultaneously
        mmio.seek(REG1[0])
        mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', pattern))
        mmio.seek(REG2[0])
        mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', pattern))
        mmio.seek(REG3[0])
        mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', pattern))
        time.sleep(0.3)  # Longer wait for coordinated unlock
        
        # Verify writes
        mmio.seek(REG1[0])
        readback1 = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
        mmio.seek(REG2[0])
        readback2 = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
        mmio.seek(REG3[0])
        readback3 = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
        
        write_success = (readback1 == pattern and readback2 == pattern and readback3 == pattern)
        print(f"  Write success: {'✓' if write_success else '✗'}")
        if write_success:
            print(f"    All three registers written successfully")
        else:
            print(f"    Readback: 0x{REG1[0]:04X}=0x{readback1:08X}, 0x{REG2[0]:04X}=0x{readback2:08X}, 0x{REG3[0]:04X}=0x{readback3:08X}")
        
        if not write_success:
            results.append({
                'pattern': f'0x{pattern:08X}',
                'description': description,
                'write_success': False
            })
            # Restore
            mmio.seek(REG1[0])
            mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original1))
            mmio.seek(REG2[0])
            mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original2))
            mmio.seek(REG3[0])
            mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original3))
            continue
        
        results.append({
            'pattern': f'0x{pattern:08X}',
            'description': description,
            'write_success': True
        })
        
        # Check XCR0
        xcr0_after = check_msr_xcr0()
        xcr0_changed = (xcr0_after and xcr0_after != xcr0_before)
        if xcr0_changed:
            print(f"  ⚠ XCR0 CHANGED!")
            print(f"    Before: 0x{xcr0_before:016X}")
            print(f"    After:  0x{xcr0_after:016X}")
            results[-1]['xcr0_changed'] = True
            results[-1]['xcr0_after'] = f'0x{xcr0_after:016X}'
        else:
            print(f"  → XCR0 unchanged")
            results[-1]['xcr0_changed'] = False
        
        # Run direct execution tests
        print("\n  [6] Running direct execution tests...")
        avx512_after = run_direct_execution_test(avx512_bin)
        amx_after = run_direct_execution_test(amx_bin)
        
        avx512_changed = (avx512_before['success'] != avx512_after['success'])
        amx_changed = (amx_before['success'] != amx_after['success'])
        
        print(f"    AVX512: {'✓' if avx512_after['success'] else '✗'} ({'CHANGED' if avx512_changed else 'unchanged'})")
        print(f"    AMX: {'✓' if amx_after['success'] else '✗'} ({'CHANGED' if amx_changed else 'unchanged'})")
        
        results[-1]['avx512_success'] = avx512_after['success']
        results[-1]['amx_success'] = amx_after['success']
        results[-1]['avx512_changed'] = avx512_changed
        results[-1]['amx_changed'] = amx_changed
        
        if xcr0_changed or avx512_changed or amx_changed:
            print(f"\n    ⚠⚠⚠ UNLOCK EFFECTS DETECTED ⚠⚠⚠")
        
        # Restore original values
        mmio.seek(REG1[0])
        mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original1))
        mmio.seek(REG2[0])
        mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original2))
        mmio.seek(REG3[0])
        mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', original3))
        
        time.sleep(0.2)
    
    mmio.close()
    
    # Save results
    output_file = '/tmp/eth_combined_3reg_results.json'
    with open(output_file, 'w') as f:
        json.dump({
            'registers': [
                {'offset': f'0x{REG1[0]:04X}', 'name': REG1[1]},
                {'offset': f'0x{REG2[0]:04X}', 'name': REG2[1]},
                {'offset': f'0x{REG3[0]:04X}', 'name': REG3[1]},
            ],
            'baseline': {
                'xcr0': f'0x{xcr0_before:016X}' if xcr0_before else None,
                'avx512_success': avx512_before['success'],
                'amx_success': amx_before['success']
            },
            'results': results
        }, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\n{'='*70}")
    print("Test Complete")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Results saved to: {output_file}")
    
    # Summary
    print("\nSummary:")
    for result in results:
        print(f"  {result['description']}:")
        print(f"    Write success: {result.get('write_success', False)}")
        print(f"    XCR0 changed: {result.get('xcr0_changed', False)}")
        print(f"    AVX512 changed: {result.get('avx512_changed', False)}")
        print(f"    AMX changed: {result.get('amx_changed', False)}")
    
    return 0

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Ethernet Controller Hidden Computing Engine Scanner
Searches for hidden unlock pathways in the Ethernet controller
Device: 00:1f.6 (Intel 8086:550a)
"""

import os
import sys
import mmap
import struct
import time

ETH_BASE = 0x7c100000
ETH_SIZE = 0x20000  # 128K

def scan_ethernet_controller():
    """Scan Ethernet controller for hidden computing engine/unlock pathways"""
    print("=" * 70)
    print("Ethernet Controller Hidden Pathway Scanner")
    print("Device: 00:1f.6 (Intel 8086:550a)")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print("\n✗ Must run as root")
        return 1
    
    try:
        mem_fd = os.open('/dev/mem', os.O_RDWR | os.O_SYNC)
        mmio = mmap.mmap(mem_fd, ETH_SIZE, mmap.MAP_SHARED, 
                        mmap.PROT_READ | mmap.PROT_WRITE, offset=ETH_BASE)
        os.close(mem_fd)
        
        print(f"\n✓ Mapped Ethernet controller MMIO: 0x{ETH_BASE:016X} ({ETH_SIZE} bytes)")
        
        # Scan for interesting patterns
        print("\nScanning for hidden computing engine/unlock patterns...")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        interesting = []
        pointer_like = []
        magic_values = []
        writable = []
        
        # Scan entire region
        for offset in range(0, ETH_SIZE, 4):
            mmio.seek(offset)
            value = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
            
            if value != 0 and value != 0xFFFFFFFF:
                interesting.append((offset, value))
                
                # Check for pointer-like (computing engine memory?)
                if 0x40000000 <= value <= 0x5FFFFFFF:
                    pointer_like.append((offset, value))
                
                # Check for magic values
                if value == 0xA00A00A0:
                    magic_values.append((offset, value, 'ENG_MODE_MAGIC'))
                elif value == 0xDEADBEEF or value == 0xDEADC0DE:
                    magic_values.append((offset, value, 'BYPASS_MAGIC'))
        
        print(f"\nFound {len(interesting)} non-zero registers")
        print(f"Found {len(pointer_like)} pointer-like values")
        print(f"Found {len(magic_values)} magic values")
        
        # Test writability of interesting registers
        print("\nTesting register writability...")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        for offset, value in interesting[:50]:  # Test first 50
            # Try writing unlock pattern
            test_pattern = 0xA00A00A0
            mmio.seek(offset)
            before = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
            
            if before == test_pattern:
                continue
            
            mmio.seek(offset)
            mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', test_pattern))
            time.sleep(0.01)
            
            mmio.seek(offset)
            after = struct.unpack('<I', mmio.read(4))[0]
            
            if after == test_pattern:
                writable.append((offset, before, 'WRITABLE'))
                print(f"  ✓ 0x{offset:08X}: WRITABLE! (was 0x{before:08X})")
                # Restore
                mmio.seek(offset)
                mmio.write(struct.pack('<I', before))
        
        # Report findings
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print("Results")
        print("=" * 70)
        
        if magic_values:
            print("\n⚠⚠⚠ MAGIC VALUES FOUND ⚠⚠⚠")
            for offset, value, pattern in magic_values:
                print(f"  0x{offset:08X}: 0x{value:08X} ({pattern})")
        
        if writable:
            print(f"\n✓ Found {len(writable)} writable registers:")
            for offset, before, status in writable:
                print(f"  0x{offset:08X}: {status} (was 0x{before:08X})")
        
        if pointer_like:
            print(f"\nPointer-like values (possible computing engine memory):")
            for offset, value in pointer_like[:10]:
                print(f"  0x{offset:08X}: 0x{value:08X}")
        
        if interesting:
            print(f"\nFirst 30 interesting registers:")
            for offset, value in interesting[:30]:
                print(f"  0x{offset:08X}: 0x{value:08X}")
        
        mmio.close()
        
        if magic_values or writable:
            print("\n⚠⚠⚠ POTENTIAL HIDDEN UNLOCK PATHWAY FOUND ⚠⚠⚠")
            return 0
        else:
            print("\nNo obvious hidden unlock pathway found")
            return 0
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n✗ Error: {e}")
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        return 1

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(scan_ethernet_controller())
